title: Add Show on PCB to the schematic context menu
description: Adds a context menu option to right-clicked schematic components to navigate to the corresponding PCB component if available.
body:
Right-clicking a schematic component, its reference label, or an associated port offers **Show on PCB** when the host supplies `onViewPcbComponent` and the circuit contains a matching PCB component. Selecting it closes the menu and passes the source, schematic, and PCB component IDs plus the reference designator to the host, matching the PCB viewer's callback-based navigation pattern.

Component menus contain only component actions. Viewer settings (ports, groups, grid, warnings), style analysis, and version information appear in the background menu. Components with no available action do not open an empty menu.

Exports `ViewPcbComponentEvent` and adds a dedicated Cosmos fixture. `AGENTS.md` instructs contributors not to edit `README.md`; this PR leaves the README unchanged. [Try the right-click menu in the preview](https://schematic-viewer-git-feat-show-on-pcb-context-menu-tscircuit.vercel.app/renderer.html?fixtureId=%7B%22path%22%3A%22examples%2Fexample38-show-on-pcb.fixture.tsx%22%7D&locked=true): right-click R1 or C1 for Show on PCB, or the background for viewer settings. The fixture displays the component requested by the callback.

Validation:
- Package build and declaration generation passed.
- Cosmos preview production build passed.
- Formatting and diff checks passed.
- Navigation and context-menu tests passed in isolation (9 tests; the existing analyzer test excluded), including component-only menus and background settings.
- All six other test files passed individually before this follow-up.
- Full type checking and the existing analyzer integration test remain blocked by the missing `@tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis` dependency; downloading it failed because the configured proxy was unavailable.
- Running all test files in one process exposes existing DOM/portal isolation failures, also reproduced with the original context-menu tests.

title: Show JLC price and stock in schematic part details
description: Adds functionality to display JLCPCB part prices and stock availability in the schematic component details tooltip, fetching data from an external API and handling loading states and errors appropriately.
body:
Clicking a schematic component with a JLCPCB part number now fetches its USD unit price and stock from `jlcsearch.tscircuit.com/api/search`. Each part number keeps its existing link and shows an animated loader until the lookup completes.

- Fetch again whenever the details popup opens, without browser caching.
- Match the exact part number and support numeric prices, `price1`, JSON price tiers, and legacy quantity ranges.
- Cancel requests when the popup closes or the selected part changes; stop waiting after 10 seconds. Failed or missing values show “Price unavailable” / “Stock unavailable”.
- Skip lookups for components without JLCPCB part numbers.

Validation:
- Type check, formatting check, and package build pass.
- All 46 tests pass when each test file runs in its own process, including loader, cancellation, selection changes, reopen refresh, failure handling, and API parsing coverage.
- A single-process `bun test` has five existing context-menu failures; reproduced the same five failures on unchanged base commit `62ae619`. The context-menu file passes in isolation.
- Verified a live C1525 lookup and cross-origin response headers. jlcsearch caches responses upstream, so displayed values reflect the latest data served by that service, not a direct live JLCPCB query.

title: Add a PCB component focus controller for cross-view navigation
description: Adds a PCB component focus controller that allows users to focus on a PCB component when switching from the schematic view, enhancing navigation and usability.
body:
Hosts currently cannot focus a PCB component when switching from the schematic view. Add `usePcbViewerController`, `PcbViewerController`, and the optional `PCBViewer.controller` prop. `focusPcbComponent(id)` queues a request until the viewer mounts and has layout, centers the edited component with padding, selects its copper layer, and draws a blue outline. Requests are acknowledged by identity so an older acknowledgement cannot clear a newer command.

This provides the destination API needed for runframe's schematic **Show on PCB** action. Existing viewer usage remains compatible.

description: Adds source_component_availability_warning for parts whose supplier alternatives cannot be confirmed in stock, retaining references and supplier information, included in Circuit JSON unions, with generated documentation.
body:
Adds source_component_availability_warning for parts whose supplier alternatives cannot be confirmed in stock. The record retains source component and subcircuit references, supplier name, and the checked supplier part numbers. It is included in the source and universal Circuit JSON unions, with generated documentation for the new record. The warning is advisory: missing data and changing stock do not establish definite unavailability. Validation: all 443 tests, type check, build, Zod lint, and snake-case checks pass. title: Add resolved connector pin 1 positions to cad_cable
description: Add optional from_connector_pin1_position and to_connector_pin1_position to cad_cable, which are absolute 3D points at each connectors mating face in circuit-world millimeters, computed by the circuit producer, to fix connector roll and identify pin 1.
body:
Add optional `from_connector_pin1_position` and `to_connector_pin1_position` to `cad_cable`. These are absolute 3D points at each connector's mating face in circuit-world millimeters (+Z up), computed by the circuit producer. Their transverse offsets from the cable endpoint centerlines identify pin 1 and fix connector roll.

Core computes these points from footprint pin geometry or motor placement in tscircuit/core#4420. The renderer consumes the resolved points in tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf#240 and no longer performs footprint inference. Existing records can omit both fields and retain legacy orientation.

Tests cover schema round-tripping, unit normalization, finite point validation, absolute/non-unit coordinates, and compatibility with old records. Validation: all 443 Circuit JSON tests pass and the package build/declarations pass.

This supersedes the closed width-direction proposal #876. No merges will be performed on the user's behalf.

title: Add parts-engine availability and price lookup interface
description: Adds optional stock and price lookup support to PartsEngine, plus an opt-in platform.checkAvailability setting for core to use it during rendering.
body:
Adds optional stock and price lookup support to PartsEngine, plus an opt-in platform.checkAvailability setting for core to use it during rendering.

The optional fetchPartAvailability method accepts supplierName, supplierPartNumber, an optional fetch wrapper, and an AbortSignal. It returns stock and a numeric per-unit price at the supplier's lowest quantity tier, with explicit ISO currency and an optional checkedAt timestamp. Unknown stock/price/currency are null; returning undefined means the supplier is unsupported. Both synchronous and asynchronous engines are supported. Existing engines with only findPart remain compatible.

Availability checks are disabled when the platform setting is omitted or false. Enabling them adds network requests and non-deterministic diagnostics. All required generation scripts were run and their updated output is included.

Validation: all 636 tests, type check, formatting check, and build pass.

Companion core implementation: https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4424

title: fix: use relative tolerance in generateArcFromSweep guard
description: Fixes floating-point error in arc generation by adding relative tolerance to semicircular arcs in silkscreen geometry.
body:
## Summary

`generateArcFromSweep` rejects exact semicircular arcs. The guard
`radius < distance / 2` is sensitive to floating-point error: the chord is
computed as `sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)`, so an exact semicircle (chord == 2r) can
land a few ULPs above 2r and collapse to a flat two-point chord.

Add a relative tolerance to the comparison and clamp the sqrt radicand with
`Math.max(0, ...)`. Without the clamp the radicand evaluates to a small
negative number and `sqrt` returns `NaN`.

Scope: silkscreen geometry only. No copper, pad, hole, or drill output
changes.

## Effect

C2652953 and C490691 each contain one silkscreen ARC whose chord is exactly
2r. Both rendered as straight two-point lines; both now render as real arcs.

## Tests

- New: `tests/arc-utils-semicircle.test.ts` (7 tests).
- `tests/arc-utils.test.ts` unchanged, no regression.
- Snapshots updated: C2652953 inline, C490691 inline.

title: repro: suffixed VDD pins lack power metadata
description: Fixes missing power metadata for suffixed VDD pins on the USB2517I-JZX component in the EasyEDA converter.
body:
## Motivation

The [USB hub board](https://tscircuit.com/gokul/usb-hub-board) uses the USB2517I-JZX imported from JLCPCB part C478081. The Microchip datasheet identifies `VDD33CR` on pin 24 and `VDD33PLL` on pin 64 as 3.3 V supply inputs.

The converter preserves both pin labels but does not give either pin `requiresPower` metadata because the current power-label inference only accepts digits after `VDD`.


## References

- [USB2517/USB2517I datasheet](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/OTH/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/USB2517-USB2517i-Data-Sheet-00001598C.pdf)
- [JLCPCB C478081](https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/USB2517I_JZX/C478081)

## Reproduction

| Pin | Current result | Expected semantic role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 24, `VDD33CR` | No `requiresPower` | 3.3 V supply input |
| 64, `VDD33PLL` | No `requiresPower` | 3.3 V PLL regulator supply input |

![C478081 schematic snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/easyeda-converter/repro-vdd-suffix-power-pins/tests/convert-to-ts/__snapshots__/C478081-power-pin-suffix-repro.snap.svg)

title: Render explicitly selected assembly.cable models
description: Adds explicit model selection to the existing assembly.cable API, allowing users to specify cable models directly while retaining existing standards and connector properties.
body:
Adds explicit model selection to the existing `<assembly.cable>` API:

```tsx
<assembly.cable
  from=".J1"
  to=".J2"
  model="adaptercable_a(bullet3_d3.5mm_gfemale)_b(bullet3_d4mm_gfemale)"
/>
```

Cableprinter parses the model and provides each end’s dimensions for routing. The original string is saved in `cad_cable.cableprinter_string`. Omitting `model` retains the existing standard inference and validation. Existing standards and connector props are unchanged.

The regression test covers a mixed JST SH/PH cable and a three-contact adapter cable with plain PCB endpoints, with one annotated visual snapshot.

Validation: all ten test shards, type checking, formatting, the distribution smoke test, package preview, and Vercel deployment pass against the released dependencies.

Uses the released `@tscircuit/props@^0.0.695`.

title: Restrict automatic datasheet enrichment to chips and op amps
description: Restricts automatic datasheet enrichment to only chips and op amps, preventing passive components and connectors from appearing in the missing-datasheet dashboard.
body:
Supplier footprint imports currently enable datasheet enrichment for every normal component, causing resistor, capacitor, switch, and connector part numbers to appear in the missing-datasheet dashboard. Only concrete `Chip` and `OpAmp` primitives now enable enrichment; microcontrollers represented as `<chip>` remain eligible. Other primitives explicitly pass `false`, including Connector and Pinout subclasses of Chip.

Geometry-only reads for footprint mismatch and orientation checks also disable enrichment, overriding engines that enable it by default. Preserve strict legacy schema compatibility, but do not retry genuine opt-out failures without the option, which could re-enable enrichment. Eligibility follows the primitive: a physical passive declared as `<chip>` still qualifies.

Validation: 58 focused tests pass covering chip metadata validation, supplier imports, connector imports, orientation and footprint checks, legacy fallback, and passive import failures. title: fix: only warn about availability for explicitly supplied suppliers
description: Only check availability and show warnings for suppliers with nonempty part numbers explicitly supplied in supplierPartNumbers props, preventing unwanted warnings for automatically selected parts.
body:
Automatically selected parts can include supplier part numbers that the user never supplied, causing unwanted availability warnings. For any supplier, only check availability and show warnings when that supplier has nonempty part numbers explicitly supplied in `supplierPartNumbers` props. Use those explicit alternatives for the check and the supplier name directly in the warning.

Regression coverage exercises every supported supplier: automatic selections do not trigger requests or warnings, explicit part numbers do, empty or blank alternatives are skipped, and removing supplier props clears existing warnings. The update test also preserves stale-result handling when explicit alternatives change.

Validation: formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Three isolated checks of the actual availability function passed with mocked dependencies, covering inferred/empty supplier props, explicit alternatives, and pending warning invalidation. Repository availability tests remain blocked by missing dependencies and an unreachable configured network proxy.

title: Add opt-in supplier availability warnings through parts engine
description: Core can now check supplier stock through the configured parts engine when platform.checkAvailability is explicitly true, providing warnings for components that may not have availability from suppliers.
body:
Core can now check supplier stock through the configured parts engine when platform.checkAvailability is explicitly true. It waits for parts selection, invokes the engine's optional fetchPartAvailability method, and emits source_component_availability_warning saying, for example, “R1 may not have availability from JLCPCB (C1525).” Core no longer calls jlcsearch directly.

- Check every supplier supported by the configured engine. For each supplier, warn only when none of its checked alternatives is confirmed in stock. Zero or unknown stock, failed engine requests, and 10-second timeouts are advisory warnings.
- Engines without the optional method and suppliers returning undefined are skipped. The setting defaults off, and doNotPlace, BOM-disabled, parts-engine-disabled, and DRC-disabled parts are skipped.
- Forward platformFetch and cancellation, share concurrent requests within a circuit, refresh on supplier updates, ignore stale responses, and remove obsolete warnings.
- The engine returns stock, numeric unit price, ISO currency, and an optional lookup timestamp. Core uses stock for warnings; the price remains available to future consumers without adding an availability snapshot element to Circuit JSON.

Companion PRs:
- https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/915 adds the optional engine method, shared stock/price types, and platform setting.
- https://github.com/tscircuit/parts-engine/pull/61 implements the JLC stock/price provider using jlcsearch.
- https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/877 adds the structured warning.

Uses released `@tscircuit/props` `^0.0.694` and `circuit-json` `^0.0.520` in dependencies and overrides.

Validation: all 13 focused availability, existing-warning, and async-render tests pass. Full repository type check, formatting check, and package build pass. The new tests cover available alternatives, unknown stock, non-JLC suppliers, unsupported suppliers/legacy engines, injected fetch, async selection, deduplication, updates, stale responses, warning cleanup, and an engine that ignores cancellation.

body:

Use published @tscircuit/modelprinter ^0.0.11. Merge current main while preserving its @tscircuit/props ^0.0.693 and circuit-json ^0.0.519 updates. Preserve main’s connector pin-1 positioning fix, generalized to each PH/SH pin count, pitch, and mating depth.

title: Compute cable connector pin 1 positions for automatic plug alignment
description: Computes cable connector pin 1 positions for automatic plug alignment, ensuring accurate alignment of cable plugs with their respective headers across various rotations and PCB layers.
body:
The docs motor/spacer/controller example renders its cable plug 90° across the board header. Core now computes each endpoint's absolute pin 1 position at the connector mating face and emits `from_connector_pin1_position` / `to_connector_pin1_position` on `cad_cable`. The original TSX requires no extra props.

PCB endpoints use emitted footprint pin geometry, including rotation and layer mirroring. Motor endpoints apply the existing assembly placement transform to the NEMA PH6 pin row. Pin 1 points are in right-handed circuit-world millimeters (+Z up); points include translation, unlike orientation directions.

Schema: tscircuit/circuit-json#878. Consumer: tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf#240, which now consumes these resolved points and has no source/footprint inference. The mesh API is already reviewed, merged, and published in jscad-electronics@0.0.193.

Tests assert emitted pin 1 points' transverse and axial mating-face offsets, rendered plug widths, and wire 1 contact order for PH/SH at five rotations on both PCB layers. Annotated docs before/after, rotation, and motor/controller visual snapshots show automatic alignment. The legacy panel omits the two new fields to reproduce the prior roll.

Uses published circuit-json@^0.0.519 and circuit-json-to-gltf@^0.0.147, which includes merged renderer #240 and jscad-electronics@^0.0.193. No pkg.pr.new dependency URLs remain.

title: Fan adapter cable wires between independent connector pitches
description: Adds functionality to create adapter cables with different contact pitches at each end, ensuring compact wiring in the middle and smooth fanning out near the connectors.
body:
Adapter cables can have different contact pitches at their two ends, such as 3.5 mm to 4 mm bullets or JST SH to PH. Keep their wires compact through the middle and fan out smoothly only within the last 20 mm at either connector, instead of spreading them over the entire route.

Choose middle spacing from the thickest insulated wire with 20% clearance, capped by both connector pitches and the declared bundle spacing. Short cables reduce each transition to one third of the path length. Add arc-length sweep samples along the existing polyline so two-point paths get the same endpoint transitions as dense paths. Preserve supplied bends, contact centers, connector poses and endpoint roll controls. Equal-pitch meshes retain their existing behavior.

Tests measure actual emitted wire caps and connector contacts, verify compact middle sections on sparse/nonuniform paths and short leads, and cover bends and independently rotated ends. Include inspected standard four-view snapshots for bullet-to-bullet, bullet-to-JST, and SH-to-PH adapters, labeled with their full model strings.

Consumer: [cableprinter #10](https://github.com/tscircuit/cableprinter/pull/10).

title: Orient cable plugs and conductors using explicit pin 1 sides
description: Adds startPin1Side and endPin1Side parameters to the cable mesh API to orient cable plugs and conductors based on explicit pin 1 sides, allowing for better control over cable geometry and conductor order during rendering.
body:
Cable plugs can render 90° across their mating header, or reverse contact order while retaining the same width axis. Add `startPin1Side` and `endPin1Side` to the internal cable mesh API: signed directions from connector center toward pin 1, in circuit-world XYZ (+Z up). The first conductor lies on that side at both endpoints.

Seed parallel transport from the starting pin 1 side and distribute the remaining twist by path arc length. Plug geometry and wire sweeps share these frames. Omitted constraints preserve legacy output.

The annotated visual snapshot compares legacy roll, a 90° turn, and a 180° turn, with full cable views and end-plug close-ups. Red is wire 1, so contact order remains visible through each twist.

![Cable pin 1 sides and endpoint twists](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/858cd402f02d7e5f81e9629ba76fa9de7ff2cf0a/tests/snapshots/__snapshots__/cable-pin1-side.snap.png)

Tests also measure plug geometry and the actual first conductor cap positions, single endpoint constraints, invalid vectors, and arc-length twist interpolation. Validation: eight targeted cable and visual snapshot tests pass; package build/declarations passed for the implementation.

Consumed by footprint inference in tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf#240; integration snapshots and contact-order assertions in tscircuit/core#4420. No new Circuit JSON fields or TSX props. No merges have been performed on the user's behalf.

title: Add component material metadata and preserve it in exports
description: Component models currently supply colors without material finishes, and the sample exporter drops material metadata. Add approximate surface materials and preserve them through the component APIs and GLB export. Share finishes for identified plasticrubber bodies, leads, contacts, copper pads, connector shells, motor parts, and mechanical metal parts. Tinned leads use metalness 0.8 and roughness 0.55 for subdued reflections. Preserve material metadata through the vanilla renderer, align React and vanilla output, and carry cable materials into previews. The browser preview uses component metalness and roughness. Keep realistic rendering disabled across CI snapshot paths to avoid its runtime cost. Restore the original test timeouts, remove extra JST supersampling, and refresh standard-rendering snapshots. PoppyGL remains updated to 0.0.34. Depends on https:github.comtscircuitjscad-to-gltfpull17. The dev dependency pins its published package preview; replace it with a released version before merging. The jscad-fiber minimum is 0.0.89. Validation: 368 tests across 243 files pass locally in 167.79 seconds, versus 360.70 seconds with realistic rendering (about 54 less time). All nine JST tests also pass after removing extra supersampling. TypeScript, formatting, and diff checks pass. Reviewed 244 refreshed snapshots. GitHub CI timing is pending. Finishes are visual approximations rather than measured optical properties. Complete PCB renders also need a separate follow-up: circuit-json-to-gltfs footprinter GLB re-import currently discards PBR properties.
body:
Component models currently supply colors without material finishes, and the sample exporter drops material metadata. Add approximate surface materials and preserve them through the component APIs and GLB export.

- Share finishes for identified plastic/rubber bodies, leads, contacts, copper pads, connector shells, motor parts, and mechanical metal parts. Tinned leads use metalness 0.8 and roughness 0.55 for subdued reflections.
- Preserve material metadata through the vanilla renderer, align React and vanilla output, and carry cable materials into previews. The browser preview uses component metalness and roughness.
- Keep realistic rendering disabled across CI snapshot paths to avoid its runtime cost. Restore the original test timeouts, remove extra JST supersampling, and refresh standard-rendering snapshots. PoppyGL remains updated to 0.0.34.

Depends on https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-to-gltf/pull/17. The dev dependency pins its published package preview; replace it with a released version before merging. The jscad-fiber minimum is 0.0.89.

Validation: 368 tests across 243 files pass locally in 167.79 seconds, versus 360.70 seconds with realistic rendering (about 54% less time). All nine JST tests also pass after removing extra supersampling. TypeScript, formatting, and diff checks pass. Reviewed 244 refreshed snapshots. GitHub CI timing is pending.

Finishes are visual approximations rather than measured optical properties. Complete PCB renders also need a separate follow-up: circuit-json-to-gltf's footprinter GLB re-import currently discards PBR properties.

title: Show dark centers on tented vias
description: Shades the hole area of tented vias at half the mask colours RGB intensity on the tented side, improving visual representation without altering drill geometry.
body:
Tented vias currently appear as uniform filled disks when soldermask is visible. Shade the hole area at half the mask colour's RGB intensity on the tented side.

Standalone and route-only vias use the existing per-side settings and owning-board defaults. Pad openings clip both the annular mask and center shading. Mask visibility defaults and drill geometry remain unchanged.

Adds top/bottom snapshots for board defaults, explicit overrides, route vias, and pad overlap, plus pixel checks for custom/transparent colours and mask-off views. Existing via snapshots and center-colour expectations are updated for the intended appearance. The mask overlay applies alpha once, preserving semi-transparent colours; context-dependent SVG paints pass through unchanged if their RGB values cannot be resolved.

Validation: 449 tests passed, with 1 existing todo; TypeScript, formatting, and build passed. Top/bottom snapshots visually inspected.

Upper row: inherited board default (left), explicit per-side override (right). Lower row: route-only via (left), pad overlap (right).

title: Keep fabrication path opacity uniform across fill and stroke
description: Fixes the issue of double alpha application on fabrication paths by applying color alpha as SVG element opacity, ensuring fill and stroke coverage is composited once.
body:
Fabrication paths with translucent fill and stroke currently apply alpha twice along their filled edges. Apply the color alpha as SVG element opacity so the combined fill and stroke coverage is composited once, preserving existing stroke geometry.

Adds raster pixel checks for filled edges and retraced strokes, checks RGBA/hex/HSLA colors and context-dependent SVG paints, and updates the visual snapshot with retraced segments.

title: Render filled fabrication note paths
description: Support the optional is_filled and has_stroke fabrication path flags introduced in circuit-json. Filled routes close implicitly and use the existing path color; has_stroke: false renders a solid region without widening its boundary. Omitted flags preserve legacy strokes.
body:
Support the optional `is_filled` and `has_stroke` fabrication path flags introduced in https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/874. Filled routes close implicitly and use the existing path color; `has_stroke: false` renders a solid region without widening its boundary. Omitted flags preserve legacy strokes.

Set SVG fill and stroke independently, retain explicitly closed legacy paths, and safely ignore empty or single-point routes.

Use the published `circuit-json@^0.0.518` dependency and its `PcbFabricationNotePath` type directly. Keep wildcard peer dependencies, following the repository's internal-library convention.

description: Adds support for GLB downloads and camera presets in the deployed renderer, resolving HTTP 400 errors for GLB format requests and enhancing the 3D rendering capabilities.
body:
Clicking the docs' 3D preview currently fails because production rejects `format=glb` with HTTP 400, `Invalid format parameter`. #2476 was merged into `feat/svg3-cloudflare-kv` after that branch's original changes reached main, leaving GLB support and camera presets out of the deployed service.

Bring the three commits from #2476 onto current main. `format=glb` selects a binary 3D model without requiring `svg_type` or `view`; image rendering stores its already-computed GLB in KV for later downloads. Includes bottom camera presets and preserves the current main renderer dependencies, CAD model shorthand support, and production domain configuration.

Validation: shared-service and SVG3 TypeScript and formatting pass; all 30 SVG3 tests pass; GLB GET/POST, camera preset, cached model handoff, and current main CAD shorthand tests pass (12 targeted tests). All CI checks pass, including production builds, Bun/Node smoke tests, the full service suite, and the SVG3 container checks. The hosted preview returns HTTP 200 and valid GLB bytes for both actual pcbstiffener docs examples, while the live SVG3 service still returns HTTP 400 for GLB format.

Paired docs PR: https://github.com/tscircuit/docs/pull/927. This service change must be merged and deployed before those GLB links work in production.

title: Add 3D camera presets, GLB downloads, and svg3 model caching
description: Adds 3D camera presets for PNGSVG rendering, enables GLB downloads without requiring svg_type or view, and implements caching for 3D models in the svg3 container.
body:
3D images currently offer a fixed camera, and requesting a rotatable model requires another conversion. Adds `camera_preset` to PNG/SVG rendering and `format=glb` (no `svg_type` or `view` required) to download the same model.

The svg3 container hands the GLB already produced during image rendering to its Durable Object, which stores the binary model in KV before returning the image. Model keys exclude camera, lighting, background, zoom, and raster size while preserving circuit input, project origin, entrypoint, method, and cache version. Images and downloads share a serialized lane, with a short local model cache covering KV propagation lag. GLBs retain cache freshness, size limits, private-request bypass, ETag/HEAD behavior, binary response headers, and CORS for viewers.

Named renderer presets are supported along with `bottom`, `bottom-up`, and `bottom-center-angled`. Both Vercel and Cloudflare adapters preserve binary GLB downloads. API and cache behavior are documented.

Validation:
- Shared service and svg3 TypeScript, formatting, and production build pass.
- SVG3 CI passes its Worker dry-run, container build, runtime comparisons, and container smoke test.
- GLB endpoint/preset and image-to-model handoff tests pass, including GET/POST downloads without a view, body format selection, and immediate downloads while KV reads still lag.
- Full service CI passes with the 30-second test timeout.
- Production smoke tests pass under Bun and Node.
- All 12 real workerd/native byte-for-byte comparisons pass; unsupported and oversized requests still defer to containers.
- Docs browser smoke testing verifies bottom images, lazy GLB fetching, orbit controls, and returning to the image.

This is stacked on #2474, which GitHub still reports as open. It can target main once svg3 merges. Paired docs changes: https://github.com/tscircuit/docs/pull/927. Deployment is required before the docs' svg3 camera/GLB URLs work in production.

title: Add JLC parts-engine availability and price lookup
description: Adds optional stock and price lookup support to the JLC parts engine. fetchPartAvailability( supplierName: jlcpcb, supplierPartNumber: C1525 ) queries jlcsearch and returns  stock, price, currency, checkedAt , with unknown stockprice represented by null. Price is a numeric per-unit quote at the lowest quantity tier, in USD. Supports numeric and string quotes, price1, JSON tiers, and legacy quantity ranges. Normalize and match exact part numbers; preserve zero stock and zero prices. Use the requests fetch override, then the engines configured fetch, then global fetch. Forward cancellation, apply a 10-second timeout, and bypass the part-selection cache so subsequent calls fetch again. Return undefined for unsupported suppliers without issuing requests. Service failures reject; callers can emit advisory warnings. Export the shared requestresult types and document the API. No new Circuit JSON availability record is needed; core continues to emit its existing availability warning. Uses released tscircuitprops 0.0.694 for the optional method and shared result types (https:github.comtscircuitpropspull915). Core consumes the method in https:github.comtscircuitcorepull4424; the warning schema is in https:github.comtscircuitcircuit-jsonpull877. Validation: all 74 tests pass, including the new pricestock, fetch override, normalization, cancellation, refresh, unsupported-supplier, and failure tests. Type check, formatting check, and build also pass. The connector import tests use a recorded C165948 EasyEDA fixture and a fixed manufacturer search result, preserving the 12-pad4-hole assertions without depending on changing live catalog results. The manufacturer test also verifies exact matching when a fuzzy result appears first.
body:
Adds optional stock and price lookup support to the JLC parts engine. `fetchPartAvailability({ supplierName: "jlcpcb", supplierPartNumber: "C1525" })` queries jlcsearch and returns `{ stock, price, currency, checkedAt }`, with unknown stock/price represented by null.

- Price is a numeric per-unit quote at the lowest quantity tier, in USD. Supports numeric and string quotes, `price1`, JSON tiers, and legacy quantity ranges.
- Normalize and match exact part numbers; preserve zero stock and zero prices.
- Use the request's fetch override, then the engine's configured fetch, then global fetch. Forward cancellation, apply a 10-second timeout, and bypass the part-selection cache so subsequent calls fetch again.
- Return undefined for unsupported suppliers without issuing requests. Service failures reject; callers can emit advisory warnings.
- Export the shared request/result types and document the API. No new Circuit JSON availability record is needed; core continues to emit its existing availability warning.

Uses released `@tscircuit/props` `^0.0.694` for the optional method and shared result types (https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/915). Core consumes the method in https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4424; the warning schema is in https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/877.

Validation: all 74 tests pass, including the new price/stock, fetch override, normalization, cancellation, refresh, unsupported-supplier, and failure tests. Type check, formatting check, and build also pass.

The connector import tests use a recorded C165948 EasyEDA fixture and a fixed manufacturer search result, preserving the 12-pad/4-hole assertions without depending on changing live catalog results. The manufacturer test also verifies exact matching when a fuzzy result appears first.

Fabrication paths currently paint each stroke segment separately, stacking alpha at joins and retraced segments. Filled paths also stack their fill and outline. Build a single nonzero fill from the filled polygon and same-winding round stroke capsules, then paint that coverage once. This preserves the round stroke envelope and works with mirrored transforms and context globalAlpha.

title: Merge coplanar faces in STEP exports and preserve holes
description: Merges connected coplanar polygons in STEP exports, reducing the number of faces and preserving holes, while allowing for individual polygon retention if specified.
body:
JSCAD exports currently create one STEP face per polygon, leaving flat gear caps split into many faces. Merge connected coplanar polygons by default and serialize their boundaries as native `AdvancedFace` entities with `FaceOuterBound` and `FaceBound` loops. A 16-tooth spur gear from models.tscircuit.com now exports 194 faces instead of 768, including exactly two planar caps with bore loops instead of 384 cap faces.

Keep boundary vertices shared with adjacent faces after T-junction splitting, preserve separate bodies and their colors, and retain original polygons when trimming boundaries are ambiguous or intersect. Add `{ mergeCoplanarFaces: false }` to retain individual polygon faces. Cylindrical walls remain faceted.

Upgrade stepts to published 0.0.4 for its native inner/outer face-bound typing. Geometry cleanup stays in the converter, in separate merging and boundary-validation modules.

Validation:

- All 19 tests (2,762 assertions), formatting, TypeScript checking, and package build pass.
- New topology and PNG regressions cover a gear-shaped extrusion with a bore, transformed multiple-hole plate, T-junctions, separate colored bodies, opt-out, and incompatible/ambiguous boundaries.

The existing subtraction PNG is updated for the changed tessellation/shading; the geometry is unchanged.

title: feat: detect resistors placed across their connected chip pin
description: Adds a solver to detect resistors placed far from their connected chip pin, providing placement advisories for improved schematic clarity.
body:
Stacked on #210.

Adds `ChipPinResistorPlacementSolver` / `ResistorSeparatedFromChipPin`. It detects a resistor-to-ground branch placed far beyond the opposite edge of its connected chip. In the speaker charger repro, R17 is across U6 from PROG; moving and rotating only R17 produces a short direct connection and clears the finding. Existing trace simplification reports nothing for this branch.

Recognition uses a typed resistor, an explicit ground net, an exclusive connection to one chip pin, its facing direction, and shared sheet/group scope. Ports explicitly marked as supply or ground are excluded. Series resistors, shared signal nets, missing ground metadata, zero-ohm links, and small offsets are skipped. Names, pin hints, net labels and part numbers do not establish roles. This is a generic placement advisory; it does not identify a programming resistor or move components automatically.

The original full-sheet repro now highlights U6 and R17 with matching numbered markers beside the diagnostic. The corrected-sheet test verifies identical electrical source records, unchanged placement of the other eight components, and a directly drawn U6–R17 connection. The unrelated R16 orientation warning remains.

[Top Power ASIC TP4056 datasheet, page 3, application 5](https://www.toppwr.com/uploadfile/file/20240130/65b892bb04a3c.pdf#page=3) shows the same PROG-to-ground branch beside the connected pin. Its pin faces right; the repro's pin faces left, so the recommendation follows the actual pin side. The surrounding circuits differ.

![Manufacturer reference beside TSX repro](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/26b79813948a900907366599350f3bd88acd5429/reference-vs-repro.png)

![Same complete charger sheet before and after moving only R17](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/26b79813948a900907366599350f3bd88acd5429/placement-before-after.png)

[Highlighted full sheet](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/feat/chip-pin-resistor-placement/tests/cases/__snapshots__/speaker-charger-resistor-repro-full-sheet.snap.svg) · [Corrected full sheet](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/feat/chip-pin-resistor-placement/tests/cases/__snapshots__/speaker-charger-resistor-placement-corrected-full-sheet.snap.svg)

title: Bundle CC2340 bidirectional capability handling in TI CLI
description: Updates the bundled converter to handle CC2340 GPIO capability metadata, allowing bidirectional pins to coexist with explicit GPIO choices and improving error reporting for missing GPIO directions.
body:
Updates the bundled converter to [circuit-json-to-sysconfig #10](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-sysconfig/pull/10), pinned to `05add591d6d678cc7457c985b08096690d1e3949`. Imported CC2340 GPIO capability metadata (`isBidirectional: true`) can now coexist with explicit GPIO input/output choices.

Before, a TSX pin with `{ isOutput: true, isBidirectional: true }` failed conversion. After, it exports the selected GPIO output unchanged. Capability-only connected GPIOs still fail with one line per pin:

```text
- U1 pin 4 (DIO11): GPIO direction is missing
```

The converter prints no additional component header or instructions for these pin errors. The CLI retains its standard failure prefix. The terminal regression tests use `toMatchInlineSnapshot()` and retain assertions for empty stdout, no output file, no generated IDs and no stack traces.

Validation:

- 60 Node CLI tests and three Bun tests pass, including both inline error snapshots.
- Typecheck, formatting and npm build pass.
- Clean tarball installation passes local and isolated global CLI tests, ESM/CJS imports, type declarations and rendering, using the minimum supported tscircuit version.
- Fresh `tsci clone imrishabh18/pedometer` (registry 1.1.3), MCU reimport with tscircuit 0.0.2747, and merged current datasheet metadata: missing directions are correctly reported for pins 4, 5, 6, 9, 10 and 12.
- In that local clone, adding the six GPIO directions already documented in the board's own interface/firmware files produces a 1,495-byte `index.syscfg`; official TI SysConfig 1.28.1+4785 with SimpleLink F3 SDK 9.21.00.36 validates the TSX and generates seven files. No request JSON is required.

This does not infer GPIO direction from datasheet capabilities or claim a complete hardware-tested firmware application. Separate from the merged diagnostics PR #257.

Remaining firmware setting outside this fix: the generated display-control GPIO (physical pin 9 / DIO20) uses the SDK's LOW startup default, while `docs/firmware-and-bringup.md` specifies HIGH. Input interrupts also remain at SDK defaults. Passing SysConfig validation does not mean those application settings are implemented.

title: Report actionable SysConfig pin errors without source IDs or stack traces
description: When ti generate-sysconfig encounters connected MCU pins without selected functions, it previously printed generated record IDs, Bun source excerpts and a stack trace. Bundle the actionable converter from converter PR 9 at commit 3da9ac4b464a84eac13615dc684da7105065c685, and report its message with a nonzero exit status.
body:
When `ti generate-sysconfig` encounters connected MCU pins without selected functions, it previously printed generated record IDs, Bun source excerpts and a stack trace. Bundle the actionable converter from [converter PR #9](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-sysconfig/pull/9) at commit `3da9ac4b464a84eac13615dc684da7105065c685`, and report its message with a nonzero exit status.

Before:
```text
Failed to generate SysConfig: SysConfig conversion failed:
14461 | throw new Error(...)
error: Unresolved CC2340 pin configuration for U1 (source_component_0, CC2340R52E0RGER):
U1.DIO11 (source_port_3, pin 4): missing or ambiguous selected function...
...
at deriveCc2340Requests (...convert.mjs:14461:11)
```

After, for two connected pins without selected functions:
```text
Failed to generate SysConfig: SysConfig conversion failed:
Unresolved CC2340 pin configuration for U1 (CC2340R52E0RGER):
- U1 pin 4 (DIO11): no GPIO direction or supported peripheral selected
- U1 pin 6 (DIO13): no GPIO direction or supported peripheral selected
Update U1's TSX pinAttributes with the intended function for each listed pin: set exactly one of isInput: true or isOutput: true for GPIO, or activeCapability: "i2c_sda" / "i2c_scl" for I2C.
Datasheet capabilities such as isGpio describe what a pin supports; they do not select how this board uses it.
```

Add `toMatchInlineSnapshot()` assertions for complete terminal errors from both Circuit JSON and TSX inputs. Also assert exit status 1, empty stdout and no partial `.syscfg` file. Include these Bun tests in the existing `test:cli` command alongside the Node CLI suite and schematic snapshot.

Validation:
- 60 Node CLI tests and 3 Bun tests pass, including both new inline error snapshots and the existing schematic snapshot.
- Typecheck and Biome pass.
- npm build and clean local/global package installation tests pass with the minimum supported `tscircuit@0.0.2745`.

This PR is limited to error reporting and its regression coverage. Pin capability behavior and datasheet metadata follow-ups are separate work. Nothing has been released.

title: fix: preserve filled PCB silkscreen rectangles
description: Fixes the issue where filled silkscreen rectangles are lost during Altium to Circuit JSON round trips due to improper handling in the PCB exporter.
body:
Altium → Circuit JSON → Altium round trips drop filled silkscreen rectangles because the PCB exporter does not handle `pcb_silkscreen_rect`. On the real NodeMCU ESP-12 board, all seven disappear: three markings on D1's footprint, three bracket bars beside D5–D8, and one bottom-layer bar.

Export square-corner filled rectangles as native Altium `Fill` records, preserving their center, dimensions, rotation, overlay layer, and component ownership. Rounded fills use `Region` records; solid outlines use closed `Track` loops and respect `has_stroke`.

Extend the existing real-board fixture adapter to include overlay fills and include rectangles in the existing primitive-count, position, and rotation checks. Refresh only the affected NodeMCU, EBAZ4205, and NEMA17 snapshots. No new test files or snapshots are added.

Validation:
- Existing NodeMCU, EBAZ4205, and NEMA17 tests pass with refreshed snapshots.
- Type checking and formatting pass.
- Independent production-importer round trip on the original NodeMCU board preserves all seven rectangles (six top, one bottom), with matching dimensions, rotations, and component ownership.

title: fix: preserve rectangular plated pad copper dimensions
description: Fixes the copper dimensions of rectangular plated pads during Circuit JSON to Altium export, ensuring accurate representation of pad sizes.
body:
SimpleFOC Shield V3 connector pads P1.1, P2.1, P3.1 and P4.1 shrink from approximately **1.8 × 1.8 mm** copper to **1.6 × 1.6 mm** during Circuit JSON → Altium export. Their approximately **1.2 mm drills** retain the correct size.

The production importer represents these pads as `circular_hole_with_rect_pad` and supplies the copper dimensions in `rect_pad_width` and `rect_pad_height`. For example, P4.1 has:

```json
{
  "shape": "circular_hole_with_rect_pad",
  "rect_pad_width": 1.7999964,
  "rect_pad_height": 1.7999964,
  "hole_diameter": 1.1999976
}
```

The exporter previously read these rectangular dimensions only for `rotated_pill_hole_with_rect_pad`. For circular drills and unrotated slots, it instead looked for `outer_width` / `outer_height`. When those fields and `outer_diameter` were absent, copper width fell back to 1.6 mm and height fell back to that width. The incorrect size was already present in the ASCII intermediate before binary serialization.

Read `rect_pad_width` and `rect_pad_height` first for every plated-hole variant, retaining the existing outer-size and default fallbacks. Width and height remain independent; drill dimensions and slot/pad rotation handling keep their existing mapping. Refresh the affected SimpleFOC Mini snapshot.

Validation:

- A complete round trip of the real Shield board through the production sibling importer and this exporter preserves copper width, height and drill size for all four affected pads.
- The Shield input above exports at 1.59999934 mm on current main and 1.7999964 mm with this fix.
- Full snapshot regeneration passed. The affected Mini snapshot also passed with updates disabled.
- Existing PCB export, slot-orientation and Mini visual checks pass: 5 tests, 75 assertions.
- Formatting and TypeScript checks pass.

The parameter documentation is in `docs/hollowpositioningarmtube.md`. Public model names, paths, examples and tests consistently use `hollowpositioningarmtube`.

title: Add radial bearing shorthand and per-face flags
description: Adds compact radial-bearing strings that expand into explicit dimensions and boolean face flags, allowing for more flexible and precise representation of bearing specifications.
body:
Adds compact radial-bearing strings that expand into explicit dimensions and boolean face flags. `ballbearing608` becomes `ballbearing_id8mm_od22mm_w7mm_bothsidesopen`; `ballbearing625zz` becomes `ballbearing_id5mm_od16mm_w5mm_bothsidesshielded`. `mp.string(source).params().string` exposes the expanded string, and `.json()` resolves six booleans with exactly one true flag per face.

Supports conventional envelope codes 608, 625, 624, 6000, 6001 and 6002. Z/RS selects a bottom shield/seal; ZZ/2Z/2RS selects both. Value-free global flags (`_open`, `_bothsidesopen`, `_bothsidesshielded`, `_bothsidessealed`) override suffix defaults, and face flags override those globals independently of order. `ballbearing625zz_topsideopen` keeps the bottom shield. Repeated/conflicting selectors, unknown suffixes, malformed units and conflicting dimensions are rejected before expansion.

Model logic and public schemas live in `src/models/ballbearing/`. title: Discover models from per-model registrations
description: Adding a model currently changes the same parser map, public export list, and definition-schema union across model PRs. This change discovers srcmodelsregister.ts at build time, so new models keep their registration and public API in their own directory. Each model exports a typed defineModel( name, schema, parse ) descriptor and a registration function. Bun generates ignored static imports, synchronous registration calls, public re-exports, and the concrete ModelDefinition schematype union. The package uses an instance-owned registry and preserves the existing exports, model order, schemas, and parsed outputs. Its published ESM works in Node and browsers without Bun. Normal test, typecheck, formatting, build, install, and pack workflows refresh discovery automatically. bun run generate:watch handles model-folder additionsremovals during development. The workflow is documented in docsmodel-registration.md; generated source and build outputs stay uncommitted. Validation: bun test (24 passing), bun run typecheck, bun run format:check, and bun run build. Additional checks cover clean generation, duplicateisolationparser-boundary behavior, deterministic model additionremoval, typed discriminants, Bun 1.3.2 hookswatchbuild, all 71 existing public declarations, 48 parser cases and 24 schema cases, and the packed package in plain Node plus a browser sandbox. The 15 open model PRs now target this foundation: 20, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 31, 33, 34, 35, 37, and 38. Each diff adds only its own model directory, tests, and documentation; existing renderer snapshots remain in those PR descriptions. All 15 pass the required checks individually. body:
Adding a model currently changes the same parser map, public export list, and definition-schema union across model PRs. This change discovers `src/models/*/register.ts` at build time, so new models keep their registration and public API in their own directory.

Each model exports a typed `defineModel({ name, schema, parse })` descriptor and a registration function. Bun generates ignored static imports, synchronous registration calls, public re-exports, and the concrete `ModelDefinition` schema/type union. The package uses an instance-owned registry and preserves the existing exports, model order, schemas, and parsed outputs. Its published ESM works in Node and browsers without Bun.

Normal test, typecheck, formatting, build, install, and pack workflows refresh discovery automatically. `bun run generate:watch` handles model-folder additions/removals during development. The workflow is documented in `docs/model-registration.md`; generated source and build outputs stay uncommitted.

Validation: `bun test` (24 passing), `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, and `bun run build`. Additional checks cover clean generation, duplicate/isolation/parser-boundary behavior, deterministic model addition/removal, typed discriminants, Bun 1.3.2 hooks/watch/build, all 71 existing public declarations, 48 parser cases and 24 schema cases, and the packed package in plain Node plus a browser sandbox.

The 15 open model PRs now target this foundation: #20, #22, #23, #24, #25, #26, #27, #28, #29, #31, #33, #34, #35, #37, and #38. Each diff adds only its own model directory, tests, and documentation; existing renderer snapshots remain in those PR descriptions. All 15 pass the required checks individually. The combined 23-model build passes 76 tests, typecheck, formatting, build, packed-package Node execution, and declaration checks.

Merge this foundation first. After merging, delete its merged branch to let GitHub retarget the dependent PRs to `main`, or retarget them manually.

body:
The powered AM3352 control now routes all 47 signals with a single `inner1` carrier under the default matched goal. Whole pad-to-pad length matching, physical differential coupling, ordinary geometry and native combined-copper DRC all pass. Every signal uses owned TOP escapes and exactly two plated vias; all 161 immutable FanoutSolver power traces, vias, pad joins and provenance are preserved.

The native pipeline derives paired backbones and timing targets from actual package geometry. It negotiates signal routes, matching banks and controls together, then releases neighboring package exits during fine-grid repairs. Independent final checks reject connected but unmatched routes. No stored signal route is replayed, and no DRC or matching tolerance is relaxed.

```ts
const solver = new BusLanesPipelineSolver(input, {
  singleCarrier: { fixedConnections: metadata.powerConnections },
})
solver.solve()
if (!solver.solved) throw Error(solver.error ?? "Routing failed")
```

Reproduce the fresh control with `bun scripts/route-control-inner1.ts`. The `control-inner1` preset is included in the standard benchmark, alongside the ten existing samples. The default and CI routing budgets are 3600 seconds per sample; explicitly supplied search budgets remain authoritative.

Validation:

- Fresh default control-inner1: **47/47**, zero combined-copper DRC issues across all four physical planes, BYTE0/BYTE1 skew **0.635000 / 0.635000 mm**.
- DQS0/DQS1/CK skew **0.048900 / 0.004720 / 0.002792 mm**, against the original 0.127 mm limit. All three pairs pass physical coupling and have **0 mm** separated exterior copper.
- Zero acute corners, sharp curve corners, illegal ordinary turns or non-octilinear ordinary segments. **94 signal vias**, **255 total**, and all fixed copper remains unchanged.
- Fresh standard benchmark workers: **11/11** completed, with native DRC, whole-copper matching and coupling passing in every sample. Successful captures were independently audited again before export. All eleven inspected PNG snapshots show every physical copper plane, including TOP escapes and fixed power dogbones. [Full per-bus lengths and runtimes](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/fix/control-single-inner1/docs/routed-am3352-placements/benchmark-results.json).
- Merged CI suite: **456 passed, zero failed**. Typecheck, build, formatting, and packed Node/browser/TypeScript consumers passed.

The fresh control-inner1 route took **1906.120 seconds (31.8 minutes)** on this machine. Search performance remains a practical limitation; runtimes vary with load. Legacy planar corridor tuning keeps its original 512-candidate budget, while the new native paired refiners use the larger budget explicitly.

[Independent inner1 report](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/fix/control-single-inner1/docs/control-inner1/report.json) · [All eleven successful, inspected snapshots](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/fix/control-single-inner1/docs/routed-am3352-placements/README.md)

title: Handle blocked signal escapes and add the full-board AM3352 SBC sample
description: The AM3352 SBC fails initial escape allocation when bottom-side pads block every local through-via site for DDR_D2, even though a native top-layer route is allowed. The pipeline now detects that condition after allocation failure and falls back to the permitted native pad layer, keeping differential partners together and preserving supplied fanout copper. The debugger and CLI reproduce the failure and a seven-decoupler diagnostic placement. Each byte group freshly routes against all board obstacles; simultaneous direct full-board search remains unresolved. Also adds a reproducible package-first workflow. A fresh outer-layer package search generates all 47 signal paths, then independent full-board acceptance checks every actual obstacle, connectivity, fixed GND copper, byte matching and all three pairs before emitting output. The captured BGA geometry, endpoints, routing rules and clearances must match; added CA constraints are rejected rather than silently omitted. Its output exactly matches the independently completed benchmark result; the complete report is committed. 24 focused tests passed (1,899 assertions), including both fresh full-obstacle byte solves, excluded-layer protection, differential partner fallback, immutable fanouts and strict package-workflow input checks. The outer-layer benchmark constrains byte buses and differential pairs.
body:
The AM3352 SBC fails initial escape allocation when bottom-side pads block every local through-via site for DDR_D2, even though a native top-layer route is allowed. The pipeline now detects that condition after allocation failure and falls back to the permitted native pad layer, keeping differential partners together and preserving supplied fanout copper.

Adds the actual astra/am3352-sbc@0.1.21 placement: 47 unresolved DDR connections, 1,111 pad/hole obstacles, and 67 immutable ground escapes, with no DDR routing cache. The debugger and CLI reproduce the failure and a seven-decoupler diagnostic placement. Each byte group freshly routes against all board obstacles; simultaneous direct full-board search remains unresolved.

Also adds a reproducible package-first workflow. A fresh outer-layer package search generates all 47 signal paths, then independent full-board acceptance checks every actual obstacle, connectivity, fixed GND copper, byte matching and all three pairs before emitting output. The captured BGA geometry, endpoints, routing rules and clearances must match; added CA constraints are rejected rather than silently omitted.

Validation:

- ./benchmark.sh --timeout-seconds 1800 --require-all-solved: 10/10 cases, each 47/47 connected with independent combined-copper DRC and planar matching passing. All 161 fixed power fanouts remain unchanged. Outer-layer runtime: 941.990 s, with 8 top and 39 bottom carriers.
- The fresh outer-layer output also passes the complete-board checker: 47 signals, all 1,111 obstacles and the actual 67 fixed GND escapes; no DRC issues. Both byte skews are ≤0.635 mm; all pair skews are ≤0.127 mm, with exterior coupling passing.
- The new package-first CLI was run end to end: 47/47 signals accepted in 923.915 s (3,752,530 iterations), with zero full-board DRC issues. Its output exactly matches the independently completed benchmark result; the complete report is committed.
- 24 focused tests passed (1,899 assertions), including both fresh full-obstacle byte solves, excluded-layer protection, differential partner fallback, immutable fanouts and strict package-workflow input checks. Typecheck passed, including the new CLI and snapshot exporter.
- All ten fresh benchmark PNGs and the completed full-board PNG were opened and visually inspected. Snapshot exporters gate output on complete connectivity and independent validation. Failed diagnostic captures remain local.

[Reproduction and measured limitations](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/fix/am3352-sbc-outer-layer-sample/docs/am3352-sbc-reproduction.md) · [Fresh benchmark gallery, per-bus copper skews, runtimes and artifact hashes](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/fix/am3352-sbc-outer-layer-sample/docs/am3352-sbc-regression/README.md)

![Fresh 47-signal routing accepted against the full SBC](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/fix/am3352-sbc-outer-layer-sample/docs/am3352-sbc-regression/sbc-completed.png)

This does not claim convergence of the direct full-board search, address/control/clock timing closure, absolute-length compliance, or via/package-delay signoff. The outer-layer benchmark constrains byte buses and differential pairs.

title: Keep fabrication path opacity uniform at overlapping segments
description: Unifies the alpha blending of overlapping fabrication paths by modifying the tessellation process to apply alpha only once at joins and filled edges, ensuring consistent rendering across segments.
body:
Fabrication paths currently tessellate each segment and fill separately, stacking source-over alpha at joins, retraces and filled edges. Union the existing round stroke capsules and optional fill before triangulation, so each note applies its alpha once. Other geometry retains its existing tessellation and blending.

Adds geometry regressions for retracing and closed-stroke holes, browser pixel checks for joins and fill/stroke overlaps on both board sides, and an updated visual snapshot with retraced segments. Includes the rebuilt distribution.

Validation: 78 unit tests, both TypeScript projects, build, the 21-scene browser visual suite, and all 597 feature snapshots pass in CI. The required SVG parity comparison reports **0 regressions across 597 comparisons**. Responsive parity layouts pass at 1200px and 480px. All CI checks are green.

Related fixes: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/pull/813 and https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-canvas/pull/302

title: Render filled fabrication note paths
description: Support is_filled and has_stroke on fabrication paths, tessellate filled routes as polygons, apply path color to fill and stroke, and add geometry regressions for various attributes.
body:
Support `is_filled` and `has_stroke` on fabrication paths, following https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/874. Tessellate filled routes as polygons, preserving concave boundaries; allow fill without an outline and implicitly close enabled outlines without adding a redundant closing segment. Apply path color to fill and stroke. Omitted flags preserve existing stroked geometry.

Update the committed distribution and the two fabrication-path snapshots affected by honoring custom colors. Their SVG reference panels remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

Add geometry regressions covering area, concavity, color/alpha, both layers, closure, disabled strokes, zero widths, and short routes. Browser pixel checks exercise fill boundaries, concave notches, alpha, top/bottom layers, mirroring, and fabrication visibility.

Validation: TypeScript, all 77 unit tests, build, format check, and the browser visual suite (21 visual snapshots plus the fill pixel checks) pass with Chromium/SwiftShader. The CI renderer test job also passes, including the complete feature snapshot suite. The base-versus-PR parity check also passes with zero regressions across 597 comparisons. All CI checks are green after the dependency upgrade, including zero parity regressions across 597 comparisons.

Coordinated renderer PRs: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/pull/812 and https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-canvas/pull/300. Enables exact SOLIDREGION imports after the producer follow-up to https://github.com/tscircuit/easyeda-converter/pull/595.

Dependency follow-up: use published `circuit-json@^0.0.518` with a matching >=0.0.518 peer range. The byte-for-byte frozen Canvas reference still targets Circuit JSON 0.0.501, so give it a separate schema alias and TypeScript project. Both the current renderer and the frozen reference remain type-checked; reference source, fixtures, and golden images remain unchanged. An integrity regression verifies schema resolution stays isolated.

title: Treat CC2340 bidirectionality as a pin capability
description: Changes the converter to correctly interpret bidirectional GPIO capabilities for CC2340 pins, allowing for proper GPIO function exports without conflicts.
body:
CC2340 datasheet enrichment marks GPIO-capable pins with `isBidirectional: true`. The converter treated that capability as a selected GPIO function and rejected it alongside explicit input/output choices. It also incorrectly treated unconfigured SWD and connected LF crystal pins as GPIO conflicts.

Before, this valid board declaration failed:

```tsx
pinAttributes={{
  pin4: { isGpio: true, isBidirectional: true, isOutput: true },
  pin5: { isGpio: true, isBidirectional: true, isInput: true },
}}
```

After, the same declaration exports GPIO Output on physical pin 4 and Input on physical pin 5. Capability-only SWD pins retain SDK ownership, and the existing crystal connectivity check still selects the LF oscillator. A connected ordinary GPIO without a direction still errors with its component name, physical pin and label:

```text
- U1 pin 5 (DIO12): GPIO direction is missing
```

Pin diagnostics contain one line per pin, without an additional component header or instructions. I2C selection errors remain separate. The converter and CLI error tests use inline snapshots.

Validation:

- 219 tests pass, including eight snapshots; typecheck and formatting pass.
- Official SysConfig 1.28.1 with SimpleLink F3 SDK passes GPIO/I2C native validation, LF crystal round-trip C/header parity, and physical pin-change checks.
- Existing configured pedometer output remains identical when published bidirectional flags are added.

This changes converter interpretation only. No new props, board preset, inferred GPIO direction, metadata edits, or sysconfigts changes. Separate from the merged diagnostics PR #9.

title: Make CC2340 pin configuration errors actionable without generated IDs
description: Connected CC2340 pins without a selected function previously produced generated record IDs and repeated instructions. Report the component name and part number, list each physical pin number and label, and provide one set of instructions for correcting TSX pinAttributes.
body:
Connected CC2340 pins without a selected function previously produced generated record IDs and repeated instructions. Report the component name and part number, list each physical pin number and label, and provide one set of instructions for correcting TSX pinAttributes.

Before:
```text
Unresolved CC2340 pin configuration for U1 (source_component_0, CC2340R52E0RGER):
U1.DIO11 (source_port_3, pin 4): missing or ambiguous selected function...
```

After:
```text
Unresolved CC2340 pin configuration for U1 (CC2340R52E0RGER):
- U1 pin 4 (DIO11): no GPIO direction or supported peripheral selected
- U1 pin 6 (DIO13): no GPIO direction or supported peripheral selected
Update U1's TSX pinAttributes with the intended function for each listed pin: set exactly one of isInput: true or isOutput: true for GPIO, or activeCapability: "i2c_sda" / "i2c_scl" for I2C.
Datasheet capabilities such as isGpio describe what a pin supports; they do not select how this board uses it.
```

Use `toMatchInlineSnapshot()` for the complete missing-function, missing-MCU-port, incomplete-I2C and conflicting-GPIO diagnostics. The regression also verifies that changing generated record IDs leaves the user-facing message unchanged. Validation still fails before partial output is available.

Validation:
- `bun test`: 217 tests and 6 snapshots pass.
- `bun run typecheck` and `bun run format:check` pass.

[TI PR #257](https://github.com/tscircuit/ti/pull/257) bundles this converter and checks complete CLI output without stack traces. This PR is limited to diagnostics and their regression tests; the newly discovered bidirectional-capability behavior and datasheet metadata follow-ups will be handled separately.

title: Use Parasolid 0.0.4 to fix native CAD hole cuts
description: Fixes artifacts in helical gear X_T exports when holes are cut in Shapr3D by updating jscad-to-parasolid from 0.0.3 to 0.0.4, which resolves issues with exterior-region chain and nominal geometry state.
body:
Helical gear X_T exports can look correct on import but produce artifacts when holes are cut in Shapr3D. Update jscad-to-parasolid from 0.0.3 to the published 0.0.4, which fixes the exterior-region chain and nominal geometry state in tscircuit/jscad-to-parasolid#3. The reporter confirmed the corrected default helical gear supports the cut in Shapr3D.

Regenerate bun.lock from npm and add a helical gear export regression for exterior-to-solid region ordering, reciprocal links, shell ownership, and nominal geometry state. The regression fails with 0.0.3 and passes with 0.0.4.

Validation: frozen installation, all 178 tests (913 assertions), the production build, and all 14 Chromium browser tests pass in CI on the final lockfile commit. The Vercel preview also passes. Local TypeScript checking and download regressions pass with the published package.

title: Merge flat Parasolid gear faces with converter 0.0.3
description: Updates the jscad-to-parasolid dependency to version 0.0.3, which merges connected coplanar polygons into planar faces for gear exports, and adds a regression test for verifying the export functionality.
body:
Update `jscad-to-parasolid` from 0.0.2 to the published 0.0.3 and regenerate the Bun lockfile. Parasolid downloads now merge connected coplanar polygons into planar faces, so a spur gear exports one top face and one bottom face while preserving its bore as an inner trimming loop. Curved walls remain faceted.

Add a regression through the site’s export path that parses the native Parasolid entities, checks both planar caps, and verifies the top face’s linked bore loop. This test fails with 0.0.2 (384 cap faces) and passes with 0.0.3 (two cap faces).

Allow 30 seconds for the existing dense NEMA export regression, matching the other Parasolid export tests; its assertions are unchanged. The first CI run completed this export in 15.9 seconds, just over its previous 15-second limit.

Validation:

- Frozen Bun install, TypeScript checking, and all 177 unit tests (904 assertions).
- Production build and all 14 Chromium browser flows, including GLB, STEP, and Parasolid downloads after edits.

title: Update model libraries and integrate HexBolt in the catalog
description: Update the models site to published ModelPrinter 0.0.10 and JSCAD Electronics 0.0.190, integrating HexBolt into the catalog with support for ISO selectors, metric size, length, handedness, and thread visibility, while updating dependencies and ensuring all existing models remain functional.
body:
Update the models site to published ModelPrinter 0.0.10 and JSCAD Electronics 0.0.190. ModelPrinter now registers HexBolt; the existing catalog would throw during startup without its adapter. Add HexBolt using the upstream schema and React renderer, with ISO selectors, metric size, length, handedness, and thread visibility supported by the existing editor and string import/export flow.

Update jscad-fiber to 0.0.89 to match JSCAD Electronics 0.0.190's peer dependency. The site uses this installed version for its model previews and exports.

Advance the ModelPrinter source pin to its published commit and regenerate the example catalog from those sources. The previous seven models remain available with their existing adapters and rendering paths. No catalog framework or model geometry changes are introduced.

title: Fix native Parasolid exterior region ordering
description: Fixes incorrect native metadata in helical gear X_T exports that caused artifacts when cutting holes in Shapr3D by ensuring the exterior region is correctly ordered and linked in the body-region chain.
body:
Helical gear X_T exports currently point BODY.region at the finite solid region and emit nominal geometry state 0. The [Siemens XT Format Reference](https://ww3.cad.de/foren/ubb/uploads/schulze/XT_Format_April_2008_tcm73-62642.pdf) (printed pp. 87–88) requires the infinite exterior region at the chain head and nominal geometry state 1. These incorrect native metadata produce artifacts when cutting holes in Shapr3D.

Start the body-region chain with the exterior void, link it to the finite solid with reciprocal previous/next links, and emit nominal geometry state 1. Bump the converter to 0.0.4 for downstream consumers.

Add native entity regressions for spur/helical gears, bores, colored multi-body SOIC models, and merging on/off. Add independent OpenCascade cylinder-cut coverage for both gear families, checking valid topology, removed volume, empty hole interiors, retained material, and equivalent merged/unmerged results.

Validation: all 75 tests, TypeScript checking, and formatting pass in CI on the latest commit. The release package build passes locally. No visual snapshots changed. The reporter confirmed the corrected default helical gear fixes the hole-cut artifact in Shapr3D; the independent OpenCascade checks complement that native application test.

[Default helical gear retest ZIP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/jscad-to-parasolid/74d6e3f1cadef9f5947c2315a043292de8aa1f1f/test-models/default-helicalgear-fixed.zip), generated with the unchanged model defaults. JSCAD gear caps currently export as many coplanar CAD faces. This converter merges connected coplanar regions with matching effective colors, extracts outer/hole boundaries, and constructs native Parasolid entity graphs. A 16-tooth spur gear with a 4 mm bore goes from 768 to 194 total faces and from 192 top faces to one top face, preserving the bore loop and area/volume to numerical precision.

All geometry-to-topology work lives here: polygon normalization, vertex welding, CSG T-junction splitting, closed-manifold validation, winding repair, coplanar region merging, and hole boundary extraction. `buildParasolidRepository` creates typed `Body`, `Region`, `Shell`, `Face`, `Loop`, `Fin`, `Edge`, `Vertex`, `Point`, `Line`, and `Plane` entities with named fields and native references, plus native RGB attribute entities. `Repository.getString()` performs serialization. `build-parasolid.ts` is a small coordinator; focused modules under `lib/parasolid/` handle polygon normalization, manifold validation, body topology, native RGB attributes, entity allocation, and shared geometry types/math. Color boundaries remain separate; ambiguous or near-touching trimming boundaries conservatively retain their source polygons. `jscadToParasolidBodies` retains its existing unmerged polygon API.
