title: Use native entity classes for Parasolid authoring
description: Refactors Parasolid authoring to utilize native entity classes, removing legacy geometry factories and enhancing the repositorys entity management and validation processes.
body:
Parasolid authoring now follows the native entity graph: `Repository` owns typed `Body`, `Region`, `Shell`, `Face`, `Loop`, `Fin`, `Edge`, `Vertex`, `Point`, `Line`, and `Plane` records connected by `EntityReference<T>`. Constructors and named properties support authoring and editing; `Repository.getString()` serializes the graph.

Remove `createParasolidFromPolygons`, `createParasolidFromBodies`, `normalizePolygons`, their geometry input types, and the polygon writer. Geometry validation, vertex welding, T-junction splitting, orientation repair, and coplanar merging belong to [jscad-to-parasolid #2](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-to-parasolid/pull/2), which constructs native entities directly. Replace geometry-factory tests with native topology/reference and RGB attribute authoring tests, and document the 0.0.3 API migration. Bulk repository construction now validates and allocates IDs in one pass, avoiding repeated scans on large authored models while retaining editable-ID validation.

Validation: 27 tests pass; typecheck, formatting, and ESM/declaration build pass. Existing lossless parsing, unsupported-schema preservation, character escapes, and entity-ID checks remain covered.

Breaking API change: callers of the removed geometry factories must use the converter or author native entities. No analytic cylinder/curve support is added.

title: Reject invalid transmitted indices and edited entity IDs
description: Rejects nonpositive transmitted indices and revalidates typed record IDs before serialization, ensuring that entity IDs are positive integers and preventing duplicate IDs from being emitted.
body:
A supported X_T record with index `0` is currently passed to `Repository.add`, which treats it as a request for an automatically allocated ID. For example, `82 1 0 42` silently becomes an IntegerArray with ID 1, so canonical serialization changes record identity. Editing a public `entity.id` can also emit zero, negative, fractional, nonfinite, unsafe, or duplicate indices because the existing checks only run during `add`.

Reject nonpositive transmitted indices before constructing records, and revalidate the typed record IDs before either serialization mode. Automatic allocation for newly authored entities is preserved; sparse and out-of-order IDs remain unchanged, and validation never renumbers records or pointers. Unknown suffixes keep their existing opaque round-trip behavior.

The [XT Format Reference](https://ww3.cad.de/foren/ubb/uploads/schulze/XT_Format_April_2008_tcm73-62642.pdf), Logical Layout (printed pp. 4-5), defines transmitted node indices from 1 upwards and reserves pointer 0 for null. These are stream indices, distinct from the separate node-id fields inside some records.

Validation: eight new regression cases fail before the fix. Afterward, all 31 tests / 126 assertions pass, including the independent framing/escape fixtures and existing native-color tests. TypeScript, full formatting, package dry-run and diff checks pass. No native Parasolid-kernel compatibility test is claimed.

AI assistance was used for implementation and tests; the diff, format reference and validation results were reviewed.

title: Compose generic adapter cables with independently specified connector ends
description: Compose independently specified connector ends with adaptercable_a(CONNECTOR)_b(CONNECTOR) to create generic adapter cables.
body:
Compose independently specified connector ends with `adaptercable_a(CONNECTOR)_b(CONNECTOR)`. For a BLDC motor's three 3.5 mm male outputs and a board's 4 mm male plugs, use `adaptercable_a(bullet3_d3.5mm_gfemale)_b(bullet3_d4mm_gfemale)`. Female board sockets use `gmale` at B.

The wrapper uses the same connector parser and composition factory for bullet-to-bullet, bullet-to-JST, and JST SH-to-PH adapters. Each connector retains its native dimensions and contact pitch. Wire insulation fits both ends and explicit contact counts must match. A/B and inner named modifiers are order-independent; reject missing or duplicate ends, malformed parentheses, positional parameters, nested cables, and trailing tokens. Remove the unmerged `da`/`db` and `diameterA`/`diameterB` APIs. Existing cable preset strings and common/bullet snapshots are preserved.

Export `parseConnectorString`, `getAdapterCableDefinition`, and canonical connector/cable serializers. The object form is `getCableDefinition({ standard: "adaptercable", connectorA, connectorB })`, with optional cross-section configuration. Physical interfaces do not imply electrical pin mapping.

Validation: parser/composition rejection and round-trip tests, mixed-family cases in both directions, existing preset regressions, local type checking, and inspected actual 3D adapter meshes. Native CI also checks the package entrypoint, gallery, formatting, and previews. Rendering uses published `jscad-electronics@^0.0.210` (merged [#427](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/pull/427)), with compact bundles and smooth fanout within the final 20 mm at each connector. The renderer preview dependency has been replaced with the npm release.

![Generic independent-ended adapter cables](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/cableprinter/357117e31695b976d578506b142f39381eb823c6/tests/__snapshots__/bullet-adapter-cables.snap.png)

Consumers: [props #910](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/910), [circuit-json-to-gltf #239](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/pull/239), and [core #4416](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4416).

Render different-pitch bundles compactly through the middle, with smooth fanout confined to 20 mm at each end (shortened on short routes). The separate adapter snapshot is updated and inspected; existing common and bullet catalogs are unchanged and pass CI.

title: Repair pinched copper polygons before Palace CAD operations
description: Fixes issues with AM3352 copper polygons that pass Shapely validity but create invalid OpenCASCADE solids due to pinched holes, ensuring proper geometry repairs before Boolean operations.
body:
Stacked on #14 (`dqs-eye-estimate`).

AM3352 copper polygons can pass Shapely validity while extruding into invalid OpenCASCADE solids because a hole touches the exterior or another hole at a single point. Guard Palace prism construction with a bounded local notch before extrusion and record the copper repairs in `geometry-repairs.json` before the expensive Boolean operations. Successful mesh summaries include the same receipt.

The three isolated source reproductions cover top GND (`U1.VSS_OSC_V11` / `pcb_trace_105` / `pcb_via_83`), bottom GND touching antipads, and inner1 `DDR_VREF`. Repairs only remove copper inside a 0.1 µm half-width neighborhood, reject any split into separate polygons, and retain the existing native volume checks.

The reusable converter and the more complete fix for generated antipad footprints are in https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gmsh/pull/1, with independent OpenCASCADE before/after validity checks and TSX/PoppyGL cross-section snapshots. This PR applies the minimal guard to the existing Palace backend; it retains its global Boolean strategy. **Full-board conformal meshing and Palace EM results are still unvalidated**, and this does not claim that every full-board Boolean/resource failure is resolved.

Validation: existing Bun suite 41 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail locally (the unchanged ngspice test requires `SI_PYTHON`); the final native rerun passes all 3 selected tests, including both existing multilayer mesh tests and the new three-case prism regression. TypeScript and Biome pass. No change to the OpenEMS or IBIS/ngspice eye path.

body:
The former CLI showed a single-frequency field and did not show what crosstalk does to a victim eye. The CLI now renders two actual TSX layouts with 0.1/0.8 mm spacing, runs native Palace broadband channels on two meshes each, and saves a geometry-first local report with same-axis quiet/switching victim eyes and added noise.

The controlled test uses identical trace dimensions/materials, deterministic victim bits, 1.6 Gb/s, 200 ps ramps and matched 50 Ω sources/loads. Quiet retains physical coupling. The transient is a causal loaded FIR approximation fitted to complex native S parameters; it is not a Palace transient or IBIS/DDR model. MIT remains unchanged; outputs are ignored and no run bundles, solver binaries or CI workflows are added.

Validation: four native channels completed (656 converged excitations); native passivity/reciprocity and the declared 5 mV loaded-voltage mesh/bandwidth/sampling checks passed. Added-noise peaks were 30.2 mV close and 3.2 mV separated. Full complex-channel mesh criteria FAILED and air/domain convergence remains unevaluated, explicitly visible in the report. These are educational results, not SI/DDR or routing qualification.

title: Validate PCB meshes and render actual AM3352 copper
description: Conformal exports previously trusted Gmshs success and positive cell quality without independently checking the saved mesh against PCB materials, interfaces, voids, and terminal paths. This reloads the saved MSH in a fresh process, rejects failed checks, and preserves diagnostic artifacts. Actual AM3352 source-via copper, rendered with PoppyGL with the substrate hidden. Red is DQS0, cyan is DQSn0; all surrounding copper is retained. Thickness is exaggerated 3 for visual inspection.
body:
Conformal exports previously trusted Gmsh's success and positive cell quality without independently checking the saved mesh against PCB materials, interfaces, voids, and terminal paths. This reloads the saved MSH in a fresh process, rejects failed checks, and preserves diagnostic artifacts.

Actual AM3352 source-via copper, rendered with PoppyGL with the substrate hidden. Red is DQS0, cyan is DQSn0; all surrounding copper is retained. Thickness is exaggerated 3× for visual inspection.

![Actual AM3352 copper without substrate](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gmsh/e4728c51c34fc282a85cb109a6b1e8bbf7d45e95/examples/am3352/mesh-validation/dqs-source-vias-corrected/copper-only.png)

The visualizer opens on this actual-board view, with additional DQS-only and native copper-cutaway views. Reproduction script and camera/input hashes are included.

## Changes

- Save physical boundary triangles and a CAD ownership/volume manifest. Validate linear tetrahedra, orientation/minSICN, material ownership, volume coverage, manifold faces, conformal interfaces, copper-net contacts, drill/cutout intersections, and actual terminal-to-terminal copper connectivity.
- Add `validateMesh`, `createMeshRequirements`, and `validate` CLI usage. Refdes/pin requirements are connectivity checks; missing PCB context is explicitly incomplete. Coincident cross-net nodes are detected even when their node tags differ.
- Add TSX-generated differential through-via/stub and cutout cases, PoppyGL snapshots, and independent saved-MSH corruption tests. Extend the visualizer with the new views.
- Add recorded crop bounds/route corridors, slab partitioning, optional Netgen optimization, and optional contour approximation with distance/area receipts. Contours remain exact by default; all copper within the analysis domain stays included.
- Retain the exact AM3352 input compressed, stackup assumptions, source-via quality comparisons, resource-failure receipts, and a 42-solid first-interface subset for further partition diagnosis.

## Validation

- 26 native tests pass, including snapshot comparisons and corruption cases for missing/disconnected interfaces, inverted/nonmanifold cells, missing materials, shorts with shared or duplicated node tags, filled drills/cutouts, and a broken inner-layer copper path.
- TypeScript, Biome, Ruff, and the Cosmos static build pass. CLI success and quality-failure exit codes verified.
- All three actual AM3352 source-via meshes pass a fresh independent recheck. The expanded crop fixes the 0.12 µm barrel-cap sliver: minimum minSICN improves from 0.000502 to 0.002009, and the new mesh passes a 0.001 gate. It contains 181,224 tetrahedra; export plus validation took 201.46 seconds. All 114 CAD solids independently pass OpenCASCADE validity.

## Remaining scope

The complete-route corridor produces 523 independently valid CAD solids in about 30 seconds, but conformal partitioning remains slow: its first stage took 665 seconds and the diagnostic was explicitly stopped during the second stage after 1,273 seconds. No successful full-route mesh is claimed. The saved subset and input make that bottleneck reproducible.

These checks establish mesh consistency, not EM convergence, air-domain boundaries, Palace port apertures, or routing/eye quality. See the [README](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gmsh/blob/validate-dqs-mesh/README.md) and [actual-board evidence](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gmsh/tree/validate-dqs-mesh/examples/am3352/mesh-validation).

Preserve layer stackups, copper outlines, plated barrels, drill voids, and dielectric materials. body:
The AM3352 Palace CAD failures were receiving invalid OpenCASCADE solids even though their 2D polygons passed GEOS validity checks. This adds a reusable circuit-json → Gmsh converter, isolated source reproductions, and TSX-generated native CAD and PoppyGL snapshot regressions.

- Preserve layer stackups, copper outlines, plated barrels, drill voids, and dielectric materials. Provide CLI/library exports, optional conformal tetrahedral meshing, and native triangle previews with cutaways and cross sections.
- Replace generated bounding-box antipads with offsets of actual per-layer copper footprints. This removes the five touching-hole artifacts in the bottom GND foil.
- Detect genuine point contacts before extrusion. Apply an audited 0.1 µm half-width local copper-removal notch, reject disconnected results, and independently validate the isolated before/after BReps with OpenCASCADE. Strict mode rejects the same inputs and writes reproductions.
- Include original/fixed AM3352 top GND, bottom GND, and inner1 DDR_VREF solids with source identifiers, coordinates, provenance, and repair receipts.

Validation: 7 Bun tests pass with native Gmsh/OpenCASCADE and nonblank PoppyGL image comparisons; TypeScript, Biome, Ruff, CLI smoke test, generated examples, and the Cosmos gallery build pass locally. The full AM3352 CAD assembly produced 5,572 solids in 288.35 s with 11.7 GiB peak RSS and matching expected/native volume. **That benchmark is CAD assembly only: full-board conformal meshing and a Palace EM solve remain unvalidated.** The original full-size Boolean exception was not reproduced in a minimal case; the independent BRep checks demonstrate the invalid inputs and the repairs.

Repo bootstrapped through https://github.com/tscircuit/create-repo/pull/88 using Bun and @tscircuit/plop per the handbook. No npm publication in this PR.

title: fix: persist PCB rendering engine preference
description: Fixes the issue where changing the rendering engine in the PCB context menu does not persist after remounting the PCBViewer, by saving the users preference in localStorage and restoring it when no renderer prop is provided.
body:
Changing Rendering Engine in the PCB context menu currently lasts only until `PCBViewer` remounts. For example, selecting Canvas and reloading the page resets the viewer to WebGPU. Save explicit menu choices in localStorage and restore the saved engine when no `renderer` prop is provided, following the viewer-owned preference pattern used by the 3D viewer.

The fix belongs in **pcb-viewer**: its `PCBViewer` owns the engine state and context-menu callback. Runframe's `PcbViewerWithContainerHeight` renders this component without specifying an engine, so it will inherit persistence after its `@tscircuit/pcb-viewer` dependency is updated.

- Use the existing safe storage helpers with `pcb_viewer_rendering_engine`, validating that the saved value is Canvas or WebGPU.
- Keep explicit `renderer` props and subsequent prop changes working as overrides, without overwriting the user's saved preference. Removing an override restores the preference.
- Preserve switching when storage is inaccessible, and retain WebGPU as the default for missing or invalid values.

title: Add cad_reference_surface records for assembly mounting frames
description: Adds cad_reference_surface records to preserve named assembly mounting frames in Circuit JSON for opt-in visualization, allowing frames on parts without CAD geometry or with multiple models.
body:
Adds `cad_reference_surface` records to preserve named assembly mounting frames in Circuit JSON for opt-in visualization. Each record belongs to a source component, allowing frames on parts without CAD geometry or with multiple models.

The record stores a rectangular shape, resolved world-space center (mm), outward unit normal, and perpendicular in-plane X direction. The second tangent is `normal × x_axis`. Optional width/height are supplied together, positive and finite, with no implicit display size. Unit-vector and orthogonality validation allow a 1e-6 floating-point tolerance. Arbitrarily tilted and reversed frames remain explicit.

Exports the schema, input type, and `CadReferenceSurface` interface; adds the record to `any_circuit_element` / `CircuitJson`. Includes generated API documentation and a lamp mounting example explaining coordinates, ownership, dimensions, and renderer consumption. Core emission and the renderer `showReferenceSurfaces` setting follow separately.

Validation: all 462 tests pass; TypeScript, Zod lint, snake-case validation, and package build pass. Regression tests cover universal-schema round trips, millimeter normalization, omitted dimensions, tilted/reversed frames, float32 tolerance, and invalid identity/dimensions/directions.

body:
Adds official circuit-json schemas for return-current excitations, spatial results, sampled fields, heatmap images, and port/via markers. Producers can reference plain or gzipped JSON through field_asset, including external and embedded data URLs, while consumers retain typed metadata for PCB simulation overlays.

All new schemas, exported types, helper APIs, filenames, and the grid-format identifier consistently include the simulation prefix.

Registers all five elements in any_circuit_element, adds pcb_return_current experiments, exports input/output types and contact/terminal schemas, and keeps spatial results separate from the existing SPICE graph-result unions. Decoded real/complex grids validate finite channels, matching null masks, and matching parent dimensions/type through getSimulationReturnCurrentGridJsonSchema. Field assets validate MIME types/data URL headers; images validate PNG/WebP assets and positive bounds.

Built on proposal #885; this PR targets main directly and includes its proposal documents until that PR is merged. Uses the existing src/simulation directory. Asset fetching/decompression, cross-document reference resolution, and SVG rendering remain consumer work.

title: Add assembly reference surfaces and printed part color/material props
description: Adds assembly.referencesurface as a typed child of generic and printed assembly parts, with named part-local planes and unit-aware center offsets, along with optional printed-part color and material properties.
body:
Adds `assembly.referencesurface` as a typed child of generic and printed assembly parts, with named part-local planes and unit-aware `centerXOffset`, `centerYOffset`, and `centerZOffset`. The default unnamed surface is `anchor`. `normalDirection` uses explicit axis directions (`x+`, `x-`, `y+`, `y-`, `z+`, `z-`); its default follows the selected plane, and incompatible plane/direction pairs are rejected.

Adds optional printed-part `color` and `material` (`pla`, `petg`, `nylon`) without implicit defaults. Includes validation and generated prop documentation.

Validation: 648 tests pass; TypeScript passes; all four documentation generators run. Runtime implementation follows in tscircuit/core.

title: feat: allow custom pin row courtyard dimensions
description: Adds optional overrides for courtyard width and height in pin rows, allowing for precise control over package envelope dimensions.
body:
Pin rows derive their courtyard dimensions from the pin pitch, which can underestimate the package envelope. KiCad's [PinHeader_1x06_P1.27mm_Vertical](https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-footprints/-/blob/master/Connector_PinHeader_1.27mm.pretty/PinHeader_1x06_P1.27mm_Vertical.kicad_mod) has a 3.1 × 8.63 mm courtyard, while the automatic pinrow courtyard for its copper pattern is 2.27 × 8.62 mm.

Add optional `cyw` and `cyh` overrides to `pinrow` and `headermodule`, including typed builder support. Either dimension can be supplied independently as a positive, finite length; omitted dimensions retain their automatic values.

The KiCad parity reproduction uses `pinrow6_rows6_p1.27mm_od1mm_id0.65mm_cyw3.1mm_cyh8.63mm` with the existing `compareFootprinterVsKicad` helper and KiCad cache. It asserts the exact courtyard dimensions, copper parity, and courtyard parity, and includes the side-by-side and boolean-difference SVG snapshots. The measured courtyard mismatch drops from 26.86% with the automatic dimensions to 0% with the overrides.

Validation:
- `bun test`: 587 passed, 0 failed.
- `bun test tests/kicad-parity/pinrow_kicad_parity.test.ts`: passed, including the exact dimension assertion.
- `bun run build`: passed.
- Biome formatting and `git diff --check`: passed.

description: Adds TorsionSpring, createTorsionSpringGeom, createTorsionSpringMesh and model-string routing for a reusable open-coil spring with two straight tangent legs.
body:
Adds `TorsionSpring`, `createTorsionSpringGeom`, `createTorsionSpringMesh` and model-string routing for a reusable open-coil spring with two straight tangent legs. Coil/wire diameters, pitch, fractional turns, leg lengths and value-free handedness flags come from the modelprinter contract. Circular normal sections and capped free ends form one closed outward mesh; left winding mirrors the same triangulation so volume is preserved.

```text
torsionspring_od8mm_wire0.8mm_turns3.25_pitch1mm_start10mm_end14mm_right
```

body:
Circuit JSON now stores PCB return-current results, sampled fields, heatmap Assets, and actual port/via markers. Passing `simulationResultId` to `convertCircuitJsonToPcbSvg` overlays one completed result on the PCB; ordinary rendering remains unchanged when the parameter is omitted.

The overlay selects the requested layer, preserves absent-copper masks, highlights the excitation trace in cyan/orange for top/bottom, and places signal/GND pad and via markers at their referenced PCB coordinates. Sheet-current magnitudes divided by the stored foil thickness give average density in A/mm², rather than a local maximum within the skin layer. Optional fixed-length arrows show current direction at the excitation current's positive peak. There is no public phase control. The legend reports the stored frequency, units, and what the arrows mean.

`convertCircuitJsonToPcbSimulationSvg` adds asynchronous embedded JSON/gzip Asset loading and an explicit `resolveAsset` callback for external assets. It loads only the selected result/layer and validates decoded channels with the official Circuit JSON schema. The renderer does not run a solver or infer missing results.

```ts
await convertCircuitJsonToPcbSimulationSvg(circuitJson, {
  simulationResultId: "simulation_pcb_return_current_result_0",
  layer: "inner1",
  returnCurrent: { showVectors: true },
})
```

The visual snapshot renders a completed Palace 100 MHz, 5 mA finite-conductivity surface-impedance EM solve over its PCB, with real signal/GND terminals, current-direction arrows, and a full-range 0–0.21 A/mm² numeric scale. The actual second-order solve has 45,493 tetrahedra and 314,698 unknowns. The 0.05 mm output cells form a 160×120 grid with 19,176 finite conductor samples and 24 masked drill samples; sampling sums the current on the exposed foil faces without filling or extrapolating missing data. Its portable Circuit JSON fixture is copied unmodified, including embedded gzip complex fields and the transparent heatmap. Source input, model/config, solver log, raw port CSVs, normalization data, and hash/sampling validation evidence trace the stored values to the solver output. The fixture documents the surface-impedance assumption and distinguishes smaller output cells from established FEM convergence.

Validation: the full suite passed (460 tests, one existing todo); ten focused tests pass, including the real-data snapshot without update mode. They also cover selection, masks/zero values, thickness conversion, row orientation, the in-phase vector component and full complex density magnitude, separate terminal positions, JSON/gzip round trips, selected-asset resolution, image bounds, a common numeric density scale replacing stored images, and explicit invalid-reference failures. Type check, package build, full format check, dependency check, and `git diff --check` passed. Uses the published `circuit-json` 0.0.522 schemas from tscircuit/circuit-json#887.

title: Route project Git clone requests to the registry API
description: Routes Git clone requests to the production APIs Git smart HTTP endpoints instead of the page renderer.
body:
Make project URLs such as `git clone https://tscircuit.com/astra/pd-power-supply` reach the production API's Git smart HTTP endpoints instead of the page renderer.

Add an external routing rule to `https://api.tscircuit.com/git/$1/$2/$3` before the existing site routes for `info/refs`, `git-upload-pack`, and `git-receive-pack`, including optional `.git` suffixes. Normal project pages retain their existing route. The API handles permissions and rejects pushes. Production testing confirmed the Git endpoints work on this Fly-backed host; the Vercel-backed `registry-api.tscircuit.com` returned 404 for Git discovery.

The schema migration (#1195) and API/cache implementation (#1194) are merged, the private R2 bucket and production credentials are configured, and the Fly API deployment succeeded. This forwarding rule is the remaining deployment step.

The API prepares packs on demand and stores their R2 object keys in the database. Its initial Git implementation exports a single latest-release snapshot commit, with no persistent history or fast-forward pulls after changes.

Validation: `bun test bun-tests/git-clone-routing.test.ts` passed (1 test, 7 assertions). Live production clones of `astra/pd-power-supply` through `api.tscircuit.com` succeeded with and without `.git`; all three clones contained the same commit and 157 files, and `git fsck --full` passed. Fetch succeeded, push discovery returned 403, and a missing repository returned 404. Clone times from the test environment were 1.76–2.07 seconds for the 8.74 MiB pack. The exact `tscircuit.com` URL still returns HTML until this PR is merged and deployed.

title: docs: correct diode example footprint description
description: Corrects the diode example footprint description to match the explicitly set footprint in the code, ensuring consistency for users.
body:
The diode overview describes a different footprint from the one used in its runnable example. The code explicitly sets `footprint="sod123"`, while the explanation below the preview calls it the default `"smd-diode"` footprint. This PR corrects the explanation so readers can relate the example code to the documented footprint without conflicting information.

## Problem

In `docs/elements/diode.mdx`, the overview example places this diode on a 10 mm × 10 mm board:

```tsx
<diode name="D1" footprint="sod123" />
```

The paragraph immediately after the preview instead refers to `"smd-diode"` and describes it as a default. That creates two inconsistencies: the footprint name differs from the code, and the wording suggests automatic selection even though the example explicitly supplies the `footprint` property.

## Change

Update the paragraph to identify `sod123` as the explicitly selected footprint. The correction is confined to this sentence in the diode overview.

## Before and after

**Before**

> In this example, the diode is placed on a board using the default footprint "smd-diode".

**After**

> In this example, the diode is placed on a board using the explicitly selected `sod123` footprint.

title: Preserve GLB node orientation through affine transforms
description: Fixes GLB reflectednonuniform node scales that invert faces or leave normals incorrect by properly composing world transforms and applying them to triangles.
body:
GLB reflected/nonuniform node scales currently invert faces or leave normals wrong. Explicit node matrices are ignored, and nested ancestor transforms run in the wrong order.

Compose the world transform as parent × local, bake positions with translation and unit normals with the inverse transpose, and reverse winding exactly once when the world transform reflects. Use the selected glTF scene and support both indexed and unindexed meshes. This keeps the existing one-transform-per-mesh behavior; expanding repeated mesh instances is a separate concern.

Stacked on #245, which supplies the shared orientation helpers. Merge #245 first, then retarget this PR to main. The canonical exporter migration follows this PR.

Validation: all 20 new real-GLB-buffer regression cases fail before and pass after. 33 node, loader, instancing, and scale tests pass. Full type checking, formatting, and diff checks pass with the declared dependencies.

title: Preserve mesh orientation through negative and nonuniform scaling
description: Preserves mesh orientation during negative and nonuniform scaling by correcting normals and winding through shared linear-transform helpers.
body:
Negative scales currently invert mesh faces without correcting their winding or normals. Nonuniform scales leave slanted normals pointing away from the transformed surface.

Add shared linear-transform helpers for inverse-transpose unit normals and reflection-aware vertex/UV ordering. Apply them in `scaleMeshByAxis` and the GLTF `transformMesh` scale path, with bounds measured from the resulting geometry. Singular surface transforms now fail explicitly. This is the first PR in the winding cleanup; loader node transforms and the exporter convention migration follow separately.

Validation: 19 tests pass across scale, placement, and rotation coverage, including 9 new tests (7 fail against the original scaling code). `tsc --noEmit`, formatting, and diff checks pass using the repository's declared dependencies.

title: feat: detect misaligned grounded parallel RC branches
description: Adds ParallelRcPlacementSolver  ParallelRcNotAligned for a unique resistor and capacitor connected between the same chip pin and ground, improving schematic readability by detecting misalignments in their placement.
body:
Adds `ParallelRcPlacementSolver` / `ParallelRcNotAligned` for a unique resistor and capacitor connected between the same chip pin and ground. In the magnetic-shutter Power repro from #217, R3 and C9 are electrically parallel but drawn end-to-end with LED1 between them.

Recognition uses native component types, explicit power/ground flags, connectivity and pin geometry. The non-ground net must contain exactly one resistor terminal, one capacitor terminal and one chip pin. It skips supply nets, shared buses, ambiguous banks, DNP parts, missing geometry and sheet/subcircuit boundaries. No names, pin labels, `port_hints`, part numbers or reference designators establish a role. The rule reports different axes, crossed corresponding ends or disjoint pin spans, while accepting ordinary offsets and unequal symbol sizes.

The original full-sheet repro snapshot now highlights R3 and C9 with matching numbered markers beside the diagnostic. A placement-only control moves C9 from `(1, -3)` to `(0, 1)`; the finding disappears and the existing R9 finding is unchanged. Tests verify unchanged source components, ports, nets and traces, all 53 terminal connections, and the other 13 placements. No unrelated existing snapshots change.

[TI LM2907/LM2917 Figure 15, page 14](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm2907-n.pdf#page=14) shows the same grounded parallel R/C connection pattern as adjacent branches. The IC, values and function differ: this supports a schematic readability advisory, not a claim about the charger's electrical design.

![TI reference beside the full tscircuit Power sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/efb5fe38bfceec105758d63a8664a8ba898d4f87/pr-parallel-rc-reference.png)

![Same TSX sheet before and after moving only C9, detail view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/30593cefb6147c1ec503f4dce5c7eb1f63c55e13/pr-parallel-rc-proof.png)

Validation: 175 tests pass; typecheck and formatting pass. Coverage includes four rotations, accepted offsets, misleading/removed names, topology exclusions, missing metadata/geometry, sheet isolation, issue artifacts and both highlight markers. The unchanged published Circuit JSON also yields exactly the R3/C9 finding from this solver; the committed repro is TSX.

Stack: #217 → this PR.

title: feat: detect spread-out diode-capacitor stage junctions
description: Adds DiodeCapacitorStagePlacementSolver, which reports DiodeCapacitorJunctionTooSpreadOut when a local diode-capacitor stage is difficult to follow because its three connected terminals are spread apart.
body:
Stacked on #220.

Adds `DiodeCapacitorStagePlacementSolver`, which reports `DiodeCapacitorJunctionTooSpreadOut` when a local diode-capacitor stage is difficult to follow because its three connected terminals are spread apart.

Recognition uses native diode/capacitor types, explicit ground flags and connectivity: exactly two diodes and one capacitor share the junction; one diode leads to ground, and the other leads to a capacitor bank connected to the same ground. It skips incomplete, ambiguous, unpopulated or cross-scope cases. Names only label the diagnostic; names and hints do not identify the pattern. This is a schematic readability advisory, not an electrical-function or PCB-spacing check.

The allowance is `max(4, 3 × largest participating symbol dimension)` in schematic units. The check allows rotations and different arrangements without requiring matching coordinates.

On the complete [E-Reader v1.0.58 display sheet](https://tscircuit.com/rushabhcodes/ESP32-E-Reader?version=1.0.58#schematic), the rule reports D2/D3/C16 once. The existing full-sheet repro snapshot gains highlights on all three components and a matching numbered diagnostic. A TSX placement-only correction moves/rotates D2, D3 and C16, and moves C23/C32/TP4 with their branch. It reduces the shared-pin span from 5.255 to 2.610 and clears the warning. All component, port, net and trace source records are identical before/after, and all other placements stay unchanged. The corrected full sheet has zero analyzer findings.

[Published reference: original E-Reader KiCad schematic, Rev B](https://github.com/IS7V4N/ESP32_E-Reader/blob/ef1aeb39f0b66f566591880b374185f5637f38d5/Hardware/PCB/ESP32_C3_EReader.kicad_sch). It shows the corresponding shared-junction arrangement; other board sections differ between revisions.

title: Resolve PCB project special strings from matching project files
description: Resolves PCB project special strings from matching project files, allowing for proper rendering of parameters like PRJ_Number and PCB_Rev in PCB SVGs.
body:
PCB text such as `'.PRJ_Number'.PCB_Rev` is currently rendered as a raw expression even when its matching project is uploaded. Resolve it from the original `.PrjPcb` parameters: PMP22712 renders `PMP22712E2`, and PMP22773 renders `PMP22773E3`.

This PR targets `main` and addresses **V01 (parameter resolution)**. The merged real-Altium comparison snapshots remain the baseline.

## Changes

- Add optional `project` context to PCB SVG rendering and associate uploaded PCB files with their project's declared document path, including ZIP uploads. Projects with different parameter values are resolved independently.
- Reuse the schematic project-parameter reader, including revision-based cache invalidation. Support case-insensitive parameter lookup, quoted/bare references and literal concatenation; prefer an exact dotted parameter name before splitting adjacent references (the review regression for `.PCB.Rev`).
- Preserve unknown/unsupported expressions and original source bytes. Keep existing component designator/comment resolution precedence.
- Download all six matching original TI project files from their pinned design archives. Update the existing six comparison tests to supply project context rather than hardcode board titles.

## Real-project coverage

| Project | Resolved value |
| --- | --- |
| PMP22650 | `PMP22650E2` |
| PMP22712 | `PMP22712E2` |
| PMP22773 | `PMP22773E3` |
| PMP23595 | `PMP23595A` |
| PMP23653 main | `PMP23653B` |
| PMP23653 planar transformer | `PMP23653-XFMR` on Mechanical 5; this board has no on-board project title |

A viewer integration test opens six project ZIPs together and verifies each PCB receives its own parameters. A separate PMP22712 repro covers full-board/layer rendering, standalone-PCB fallback, a same-named unrelated board, and untouched source round trips.

## Comparisons and scope

The left panels retain the original Altium reference bytes and crops. Only resolved text values change in the right-hand PCB SVGs; an XML comparison against `main` confirms identical element attributes and geometry. Each TI panel is labeled as using matching project parameters.

**Font size and text placement remain separate V02/V03 issues (#245 and #243).** Consequently the PMP22712 title is still shifted/clipped and PMP22773 text placement still differs from Altium. This PR resolves the string value; it does not claim complete text-rendering parity.

A standalone PCB cannot supply parameters stored only in its project. Some existing standalone Altium 365 reference captures (PMP23595/PMP23653 main) therefore retain raw expressions on the left; their AltiumTS panels now receive the matching original project. No reference pixels are altered.

body:
Existing PCB snapshots show only AltiumTS output, which makes differences from Altium difficult to review. This replaces **27 existing snapshot files** with real Altium on the left and the original test's AltiumTS output on the right. The two extra PMP comparison snapshots are removed; comparisons now use the original snapshot filenames.

This is a comparison baseline. Production rendering code, source documents, renderer options, and existing geometry assertions are unchanged.

### Coverage

The corpus contains **46 PCB snapshots: 27 comparisons and 19 still awaiting usable references**. A checked inventory covers every existing PCB snapshot and fails if a case is omitted.

| Board | Captured views |
| --- | --- |
| C17 | Full PCB, top solder |
| DSP5509 CIII | Full design including off-board components |
| Elk Pi | Full, top copper, overlay, bottom routing, inner pad stack, polygon cutout, roundrect pads, slots, rotated pads |
| Novena eDP | Full, component bodies, U10C, AUX net, paste detail, solder detail |
| STM32 ST-Link V2 | Full, mechanical layer 7 |
| TI power boards | PMP22650, PMP22712, PMP22773, PMP23595, PMP23653 main and planar transformer |
| AM62L | Top copper, text hidden; existing golden output caveat below |

PMP22712/PMP22773 use the original uploaded Altium screenshots. Other references were captured in the official Altium 365 Viewer from the exact PCB documents consumed by these tests. Metadata records source/screenshot hashes, image format, dimensions, layers, and crop alignment. Tests verify the unchanged embedded image bytes. Detail crops retain the captured raster resolution; Altium's component/net selection dims unrelated primitives whereas the existing AltiumTS tests filter them out.

### Remaining limitations

- **8 real-board views** (CH582, Sample Board, SimpleFOC Shield, and five SimpleFOC Mini views): the official viewer rejected the original ASCII documents in single-board ZIPs. Safe binary serialization cannot preserve all their records.
- **11 synthetic cases**: the generated native fixtures did not produce usable viewer renders, or native serialization is unsupported. The original tests/snapshots remain intact, with concrete blockers in `coverage.json`. These need native Altium reference captures.
- **AM62L's renderer test did not complete within 120 seconds.** Its real Altium reference is captured, but the right panel wraps the existing checked-in golden SVG. The image explicitly labels this limitation; it is not a newly validated renderer result.

Capture provenance, the full inventory, and regeneration instructions are in [board-comparisons.md](https://github.com/tscircuit/altiumts/blob/66887f18e4cf35b52af9de576e535a54e3266b92/tests/fixtures/altium-reference/board-comparisons.md) and [coverage.json](https://github.com/tscircuit/altiumts/blob/66887f18e4cf35b52af9de576e535a54e3266b92/tests/fixtures/altium-reference/coverage.json).

### Elk Pi baseline verification

The review's apparent pad deletion is an SVG ordering change inherited from the base renderer. Both Elk Pi comparison panels were regenerated independently from base commit `4cf4aad7357c733b72dd85f97fdfeab70e4ba502`; that output is byte-for-byte identical to the embedded AltiumTS panels.

- Bottom routing retains all **42 pads, including all 20 MULTILAYER pads**. Its entire SVG-line multiset matches the old golden; only paint order differs. The test now asserts both pad counts so missing hidden pads cannot pass unnoticed.
- The middle-layer polygon is an existing `MID1` outline with `fill="none"`, outside the 120-by-120 crop. The old golden omitted this markup, but the base renderer already emits it.
- Raster comparisons against the original goldens found **zero changed pixel channels** in both views. The pixel-based snapshot matcher retains old markup when rendered pixels match, explaining why these changes first appeared when the comparison wrappers were generated.
- Moved `escapeXml` to module scope to follow the named-closure guidance. No snapshots or production code changed in this review follow-up.

The fixture hash and fresh base-render SVG hashes are recorded in `board-comparisons.md` for reproduction.

### Validation

- `bun run download-references` passed.
- Suite excluding the three existing AM62L cases: **349 passed, 0 failed, 3 filtered out**.
- Reference inventory/image validation: **3 passed**; focused review run including both Elk Pi views: **6 passed**.
- Library and site typechecks, formatting, lint, library build, site build, and `git diff --check` passed.
- All 27 comparison images visually reviewed. Separate AM62L renderer attempt timed out at 120 seconds, as noted above.

### Examples

PMP22712, retaining the current unresolved text for comparison:

![PMP22712 real Altium and AltiumTS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/altiumts/66887f18e4cf35b52af9de576e535a54e3266b92/tests/svg/__snapshots__/ti-pmp22712-pcb.snap.svg)

title: Preserve TI sheet 23 DIP-switch details and rotated resistor labels
description: Preserves the internal actuators of DIP switches and maintains the correct orientation of resistor labels during conversion from Altium to Circuit JSON.
body:
TI TMDS62LEVM Rev. B sheet 23 loses the internal actuators of SW4, SW2, and SW3 during conversion. Its tightly spaced pull-up resistors also get horizontal native-symbol labels that collide, although Altium places those labels vertically.

Preserve the original multi-rectangle switch bodies and their labels. For resistors with rotated visible labels, preserve the source body and pin geometry when the graphics form a complete path between both pins; keep the native fallback for incomplete graphics. Convert Altium's counterclockwise text angles to SVG screen-space rotation so the preserved labels face the correct direction and clear the switch pin numbers.

Update all 12 affected schematic snapshots, including other sheets with the same rotated resistor or imported-text behavior.

### Before

![Missing switch internals and colliding resistor labels](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Devesh36/altium-to-circuit-json/8e6acf45b0b28b19de93c672d9333137a6fb96aa/sheet23-before.png)

### After

![Preserved DIP-switch internals and readable vertical resistor labels](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Devesh36/altium-to-circuit-json/8e6acf45b0b28b19de93c672d9333137a6fb96aa/sheet23-after.png)

### Validation

- 232 conversion tests and all 83 schematic tests passed, including snapshot comparisons.
- Regression tests cover all three DIP switches, all eight pull-up resistor layouts and connected terminals, text enabled/disabled, line/polyline resistor bodies, and hidden/inactive/incomplete fallback cases.
- Custom-body tests distinguish mixed polygon/polyline bodies from single-kind decoration and insufficient graphics.
- All four text orientations are compared against Altium's own SVG output; existing gate overbar tests use the corrected rotation.
- Architecture checks, typecheck, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Symbol/body selection is extracted into a helper to keep `convertComponent.ts` within the handbook file-size limit.

title: Preserve complete custom symbols instead of generic boxes
description: Preserves complete custom symbols for LM5155 U3 and D4, and LMG342X potentiometers by recognizing filled polygons and supporting polylines, ensuring the identity and electrical meaning of components are maintained during conversion.
body:
**Motive:** Replacing a device-specific schematic with a generic box hides the component’s identity and electrical meaning.

LM5155 U3 (LMV431) and D4, as well as the LMG342X potentiometers, have complete Altium bodies built from filled polygons and supporting polylines, but the converter grouped both record types into one primitive family and rejected those bodies. This change recognizes a filled polygon plus sufficient body primitives as evidence of a complete custom symbol, preserving the source geometry while leaving sparse decorations and existing native-symbol selection alone. Regression tests assert the recovered bodies for U3, D4, R3, and R15, and the two affected SVG snapshots are updated; all 83 schematic snapshot tests and 212 conversion and architecture tests pass, along with typecheck and formatting checks.

title: Preserve LM5155 U3 shunt-reference symbol graphics
description: Fixes rendering issue where LM5155EVM-FLY U3 was displayed as a generic box instead of its original shunt-reference symbol due to custom-body heuristic limitations.
body:
LM5155EVM-FLY U3 (`LMV431BIMF/NOPB`) was rendered as a generic box even though Altium contains its shunt-reference triangle, cathode bar, and reference lead. The custom-body heuristic grouped polygons and polylines into one primitive kind, so it rejected the complete symbol.

Count closed polygons and open polylines separately while retaining the existing minimum of three primitives and two kinds. This preserves U3's original graphics and label placement without moving its three connected pins. The same correction preserves the two potentiometer bodies (R3 and R15) in LMG342X-BB-EVM; both affected schematic snapshots are updated.

### Before

![U3 rendered as a generic box](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Devesh36/altium-to-circuit-json/4e687b1ebe59f37f73f039c9bdf4162b60f7f009/u3-before.png)

### After

![U3 with its original shunt-reference symbol](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Devesh36/altium-to-circuit-json/4e687b1ebe59f37f73f039c9bdf4162b60f7f009/u3-after.png)

### Validation

- 209 conversion tests passed; 83 schematic tests passed, including all schematic snapshot comparisons.
- Regression coverage checks U3's source geometry and all three trace connections, with text enabled and disabled; insufficient graphics still use the box fallback.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, and `git diff --check` passed.

title: Fix reversed diode polarity in converted schematics
description: Fixes the reversed diode polarity in converted schematics to ensure correct representation of anode and cathode terminals, preventing misinterpretation of circuit functionality.
body:
**Motive:** A diode drawn with its cathode on the wrong side reverses the circuit’s meaning for anyone reading the converted schematic.

Altium LM5155 D2 names pin 1 K and pin 2 A, while the native diode symbols associate numeric pin 1 with the positive terminal and pin 2 with the negative terminal; the previous numeric-first match therefore moved the cathode bar from left to right. This change gives diode terminal names (A/anode and K/cathode) precedence when assigning symbol ports, while retaining numeric matching for diodes without meaningful terminal names and preserving the original pin numbers and connections. Regression tests cover both orientations, named and numeric-only pins, and the LM5155 net-connected ports; all 83 schematic snapshot tests and 202 conversion and architecture tests pass, and the affected snapshots are updated.

title: Preserve collapsed solder-mask openings
description: Maps Altium solder-mask expansions that fully close an opening to Circuit JSONs existing covered-pad representation instead of emitting an invalid negative radius.
body: Maps Altium solder-mask expansions that fully close an opening to Circuit JSON's existing covered-pad representation instead of emitting an invalid negative radius. Reproduces the failure with the LM251772EVM-PD source and updates the affected 3D snapshots.\n\nAll 185 conversion tests pass.

title: Preserve embedded Altium CAD models
description: Converts embedded Altium STEP bodies into Circuit JSON CAD components using their source position, board side, height, and rotation. All 228 models across the five TI EVM repros are checked individually and rendered in top and bottom 3D snapshots.
body: Converts embedded Altium STEP bodies into Circuit JSON CAD components using their source position, board side, height, and rotation. All 228 models across the five TI EVM repros are checked individually and rendered in top and bottom 3D snapshots.

body: Adds one visual repro per TI EVM. Each source Altium file contains positioned embedded STEP bodies, while the converted Circuit JSON contains no CAD models; top and bottom 3D snapshots make the loss visible.

title: Preserve graphical polarity on curved-plate capacitors
description: Fixes the graphical representation of polarized capacitors with curved plates in the schematic conversion process, ensuring accurate rendering of their polarity regardless of how the  sign is represented.
body:
## Problem

PR #178 preserves polarized capacitor graphics when the Altium body contains a visible text `+`. Some polarized capacitors draw the plus with primitives rather than text. SimpleFOC Mini C3 uses two filled rectangles for `+` and two elliptical arcs for its curved plate; the current converter replaces that body with an ordinary flat-plate capacitor. The same curved-plate pattern appears on SimpleFOC Shield C6, DRV8307 C1, and LM5155 C2.

## Fix

When an ordinary native capacitor would be selected, treat a visible source arc paired with a straight line or polyline as evidence of a curved capacitor plate. Preserve the complete source body using the existing custom-body converter, keeping the plate, graphical polarity mark, and original terminal positions. This extends #178's text-label detection without part-number exceptions. Already recognized polarized native symbols retain their existing path, and incomplete source bodies still use the native fallback.

## Validation

- Regression test on the real SimpleFOC Mini C3 fixture checks its two curved-plate arcs, two filled `+` shapes, and two electrical ports.
- Synthetic tests cover a curved plate without a text marker and ordinary capacitors without a curved plate.
- Refreshed eight affected schematic snapshots: SimpleFOC Mini, SimpleFOC Shield V3, DRV8307EVM, LM5155EVM-FLY, and TI TMDS62LEVM sheets 14, 20, 39, and 40. Inspected SimpleFOC Mini C3 and the TI sheets visually.
- `bun test tests/conversion tests/svg/arduino-uno-schematic.test.ts tests/svg/nodemcu-esp12-schematic.test.ts tests/svg/simplefocmini-schematic.test.ts` (200 pass); `bun run typecheck`; Biome check of changed TypeScript files.

title: Fix lost capacitor polarity marks and curved plates in schematic conversion
description: Fixes loss of capacitor polarity marks and curved plates during schematic conversion for Arduino Uno components C1 and C2.
body:
## Problem

Arduino Uno C1 and C2 have a curved capacitor plate and an explicit `+` mark in the Altium source. Conversion replaces both with an ordinary capacitor symbol, losing the polarity information. Their library reference is a manufacturer part number, so the existing name-based polarized-capacitor detection does not recognize them.

## Fix

When native selection would use an ordinary capacitor but the active source body contains a visible `+` label, preserve its graphics through the existing custom-body converter. This retains the curved plate, polarity mark, and original terminal positions without assuming that pin 1 must be positive.

Already-recognized polarized symbols retain their existing behavior. Hidden labels, inactive component parts, and parameter values do not trigger the fallback; incomplete source bodies keep the native symbol. The production change is confined to component conversion, with no component-name or manufacturer-part-number exceptions.

## Validation

- Added synthetic coverage for reversed pin numbering, text-disabled conversion, hidden/inactive marks, parameter text, and incomplete graphics. The two preservation cases fail against the original converter.
- Added an Arduino regression asserting both polarity marks, curved plates, and electrical connections.
- Refreshed the affected Arduino and NodeMCU schematic snapshots and visually inspected Arduino C1/C2.
- TypeScript type checking and Biome checks pass for the changed TypeScript files.

- All 95 tests across 17 schematic/conversion test files passed; a separate run without snapshot updates passed all 11 focused regression and affected-snapshot checks.

title: Fix overly thick schematic component strokes
description: Fixes overly thick strokes in schematic components by scaling stroke widths according to document scale and decoding Altium TSize widths correctly.
body:
## Motivation

Small component details in the Circuit JSON rendering of `ti-drv8307evm-schematic.snap.svg` appear much thicker and darker than their Altium counterparts. Connector outlines and contact circles, transistor graphics, and custom gate bodies lose definition because their strokes do not shrink with the sheet geometry.

The converter imposed a `0.05` minimum stroke width on schematic primitives and owned component pins. On DRV8307EVM, a one-unit source stroke should scale to approximately `0.01666`, so the minimum made it about three times too thick. It also interpreted Altium's `LINEWIDTH` enum as a literal length.

## Changes

- Scale primitive and owned-pin strokes with the existing document scale, removing the fixed minimum.
- Decode Altium TSize widths as hairline / 10 / 30 / 50 mils, using the source-unit mapping `[1, 1, 3, 5]`. Hairlines use one source unit because Circuit JSON has no device-pixel stroke representation.
- Add seven regression cases covering default and explicit width settings, fallback handling, multiple primitive types, and custom component pins at different scales.
- Refresh schematic SVG snapshots for the shared rendering change.

The production change is limited to two existing functions and applies to all imported symbols without component names, fixture-specific conditions, or color changes.

## Validation

- 83 schematic and component-body tests passed with refreshed snapshots.
- All seven new regression tests fail against the original implementation and pass with the fix.
- After rebasing onto current main: 19 tests passed, covering the DRV8307 snapshot, stroke regressions, and upstream hidden-parameter regression.
- TypeScript type checking and Biome checks for the three changed TypeScript files passed.
- Visually inspected the DRV8307 connector and custom-symbol details before and after conversion.

Large fixture tests were run with a 120-second timeout after the default five-second limit caused local timeouts. The full PCB suite was not completed. Some existing snapshots also had pre-existing text/rendering differences when regenerated; the Circuit JSON comparison for the inspected hardware fixture confirmed that this code change only alters stroke widths.

title: Add adhesive-mount electrical component heatsink model contract
description: Adds a new model contract for an adhesive-mount electrical component heatsink, defining its dimensions and properties for integration into the modelprinter.
body:
Adds `adhesivemountelectricalcomponentheatsink` for rectangular plate-fin heatsink bodies intended to bond to electrical components with adhesive or thermal tape. Width, length, total height, base thickness, fin thickness and count define equally spaced fins and a flat Z=0 bonding face. Adhesive is a separate assembly part and is excluded from the body's dimensions and volume; the model specifies no thermal or insulation rating.

```text
adhesivemountelectricalcomponentheatsink_w20mm_l25mm_h12mm_base2mm_fin1mm_fins6
```

The public schemas, `AdhesiveMountElectricalComponentHeatsinkModelPropsInput` and related types, parser, `getAdhesiveMountElectricalComponentHeatsinkDimensions`, and typed registration live in the model's own folder. Validation rejects ambiguous tokens, invalid dimensions, noninteger fin counts and closed fin gaps.

Validation: 137 tests pass with Bun 1.3.2; typecheck, formatting, build and `git diff --check` pass.

### Renderer and snapshots

[jscad-electronics #444](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/pull/444) consumes this contract through the published preview at `4fb94f8`. Its checked-in snapshots show the complete model string and ISOMETRIC / TOP / FRONT / SIDE views. Geometry and PNGs remain in the renderer repository.

**Standard six-fin body, 20 × 25 × 12 mm.**

![Adhesive-mount electrical component heatsink — standard four-view snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/62ffd143e73a265c22cf30eb63f2defd7de7e478/tests/snapshots/__snapshots__/adhesivemountelectricalcomponentheatsink-standard.snap.png)

**Compact four-fin body, 7 × 6 × 7 mm.**

![Adhesive-mount electrical component heatsink — compact four-view snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/62ffd143e73a265c22cf30eb63f2defd7de7e478/tests/snapshots/__snapshots__/adhesivemountelectricalcomponentheatsink-compact.snap.png)

The renderer remains a draft until this contract is merged and its preview dependency is replaced with a stable modelprinter release.

title: Add compatible mechanical model-string flag syntax
description: Mechanical model strings now accept value-free flags such as _setscrew, _singleclamp, _lefthanded, _closedground, and driveprofileshape flags, allowing for a more streamlined syntax while maintaining legacy support.
body:
Mechanical model strings now accept value-free flags such as `_setscrew`, `_singleclamp`, `_lefthanded`, `_closedground`, and drive/profile/shape flags. For example, `shaftcollar_bore8mm_od16mm_w8mm_setscrew_m4_lefthanded` produces the same JSON as the released `mount(setscrew)` / `threadhand(left)` syntax.

Aliases and default omission rules live beside each model. Only new flag strings normalize; legacy strings retain their raw `.params()` and deferred validation. Existing JSON schemas and renderer-facing enum fields remain unchanged. Mixed legacy/new selectors and duplicate or conflicting flags fail before normalization can erase them. Standards, metric sizes, and tolerance classes retain their identifier syntax.

Documents supported aliases and validation behavior.

Validation:
- All 134 tests pass, including 43 flag/legacy equivalence cases; typecheck, format check, build, and npm pack pass.
- All 92 existing public declaration files and root runtime exports match published modelprinter 0.0.17. Legacy raw params and JSON match the published package for every alias fixture.
- Current jscad-electronics main (0.0.213) typechecks and builds against the packed candidate. Ordinary Node checks all 43 aliases through both React and vanilla renderers; each produces identical geometry and materials to its legacy string. Threaded-rod geometry fixtures use a 10 mm length while parser comparisons cover the original 100 mm strings.
- Three representative models export valid GLBs and render in Chromium WebGL without page errors or blank canvases: set-screw shaft collar, left-handed compression spring, and plain bushing.
- GitHub CI test job passed.

No auto-merge.

Preview publishing: the first pkg-pr-new attempt failed with a network `fetch failed` after its build passed. Retried the preview job; this is separate from the successful CI test job.

title: Add open-coil torsion spring model contract
description: Adds a reusable torsionspring contract for an open helical coil with two straight tangent legs, defining its dimensions and properties.
body:
Adds a reusable `torsionspring` contract for an open helical coil with two straight tangent legs. Coil/wire diameters, pitch, fractional turns and independent leg lengths define the free-state envelope. Value-free `_left` / `_right` flags select winding; frame and dimension helpers expose a shared centerline and circular normal-section datums.

```text
torsionspring_od8mm_wire0.8mm_turns3.25_pitch1mm_start10mm_end14mm_right
```

The coil advances along +Z from `(meanRadius,0,0)`. Legs extend the exact helical tangent, including its axial slope; they are not constrained to XY end planes. Fractional turns set the terminal phase. This is a generic open-coil reference, not a closed-wound spring, supplier part or spring-rate/preload model.

Schemas normalize lengths to millimeters, resolve pitch from wire diameter when omitted, and reject ambiguous hand flags, duplicate/unknown tokens, invalid bore/coil gaps and nonfinite dimensions. The model uses folder-local typed registration and does not change central dispatch or generated source.

Validation: all 84 tests pass with Bun 1.3.2, including defaults/units, schema roundtrips, handedness, continuous orthonormal frames and invalid inputs. Typecheck, format check, build and `git diff --check` pass. The installed Bun 1.3.14 reproduces the existing temporary-module discovery failure previously identified on main. No README, generated files, meshes, renderer dependencies or lockfile changes.

### Renderer and generated snapshots

Implemented in [jscad-electronics #443](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/pull/443). Both checked-in PNGs use the shared four-view renderer and label their full model strings. Images are pinned to renderer commit `86f0867`; meshes and PNG files stay in jscad-electronics.

**Right-hand spring.**

![Right-hand spring — four rendered views](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/86f0867d84db6f5c5780e6b6500c9bce62b1a9a5/tests/snapshots/__snapshots__/torsionspring-right.snap.png)

**Left-hand spring.**

![Left-hand spring — four rendered views](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/86f0867d84db6f5c5780e6b6500c9bce62b1a9a5/tests/snapshots/__snapshots__/torsionspring-left.snap.png)

The renderer draft pins this contract PR’s published preview package. Replace that dependency with a stable modelprinter release after this contract merges and before the renderer merges.

title: render explicit soldermask openings in webgpu
description: Fixes the ignored soldermask opening that was previously unsupported, ensuring that the opening exposes copper while the surrounding mask remains intact.
body:
### Motivation
- Fix the ignored soldermask opening reproduced in #23. Stacked on #23; merge the repro first.

### Before
- The three-element repro reports an unsupported opening and leaves the copper covered.
- ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/294fdc30691bc82d759ce66bb0369d8a927b5301/tests/snapshots/soldermask-opening.png)

### After

title: Prototype Circuit JSON CLI and surface-impedance return-current EM
description: Prototype Circuit JSON inputoutput for return-current simulations using the merged schemas from circuit-json887, including an explicit finite-conductivity EM boundary model for supported two-layer boards.
body:
Prototype Circuit JSON input/output for return-current simulations using the merged schemas from [circuit-json#887](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/887), including an explicit finite-conductivity EM boundary model for supported two-layer boards.

The CLI selects a pending `pcb_return_current` experiment or creates one from named source/load/reference/current flags. Completed Palace runs output the complete board plus official result, complex field, transparent heatmap and actual PCB port/via markers. The approximation emits a real field without a frequency; Palace requires an explicit frequency and physical stackup where applicable.

Embedded plain/gzipped fields use A/mm sheet currents, bottom-left row order, shared null conductor masks and peak `exp(+jωt)` phasors. Reruns replace only the selected experiment/frequency and its result descendants. Export rejects stale input/model/current/contact/termination/provenance, mismatched copper modes and incomplete conductor masks. Opposite-direction experiments preserve original PCB routes and orient a separate solver view. Legacy point-only APIs remain supported.

Definition/selection helpers stay in the browser-compatible main entry. The Node-only exporter lives at `simulate-return-current/circuit-json`; gzip and native PNG rendering are excluded from the Cosmos browser bundle.

`--copper-model surface_impedance` explicitly selects Palace's half-space finite-conductivity boundary model. The physical foil, drills and plated barrels are preserved, copper volumes are subtracted from the solve domain, and their exterior receives `Boundaries.Conductivity` with the physical conductivity and `External: true`. The importer sums actual complex `J_s` coefficients on exposed ground-foil faces and applies the existing source-current normalization. Model/reference/receipts label this `surface_impedance_copper`; volumetric copper remains the default. The surface model requires foil and wall thickness ≥3 skin depths and rejects multilayer geometry. It does not claim a resolved copper-volume skin-depth mesh.

Validation:

- Full suite: 40 passing; all five optional Gmsh/VTK checks also passed separately, including equal CAD copper volume, finite-conductivity boundaries, retained port resistances, complex signed face summation, one-face via junctions, float32 VTK plane coordinates and rejection outside actual faces.
- Typecheck, package build, Cosmos site build, format check and installed Node CLI/library/NodeNext smoke check, including 100 MHz surface-mode preparation from a pending Circuit JSON definition and the packaged Python importer.
- Actual Palace v0.14.0 integration at 1 MHz: explicit U1/U2 signal/GND terminals, 5 mA peak, source 25 Ω/load 100 Ω, 80×60 complex field/eight drill masks. This coarse order-1 integration fixture is not an accuracy reference.
- Actual Palace v0.14.0 integration at 100 MHz: unchanged board/terminals, 35 µm foil and barrel walls, conductivity 5.8e7 S/m, explicit half-space surface impedance (5.30 skin depths), P2, 45,493 tetrahedra/314,698 unknowns. The 0.05 mm sample grid is 160×120 with 19,176 conductor cells and 24 drill masks; 24 annulus cells correctly have one exposed foil face. Official schemas, embedded assets, complete masks and exact field/reference equality pass. Source current normalizes to 5 mA; input impedance is 100.01625+j0.391499 Ω, with positive input/load power. [Actual result and compact evidence](https://github.com/tscircuit/return-current-trace-demo/tree/main/examples/circuit-json) are archived in the demo repository. Mesh/domain/local-density convergence has not been established.

This remains a draft prototype alongside the demo adapters and Circuit JSON rendering prototype. Frequency/solver/fabrication settings remain run options because PR887 does not define them on pending experiment records. The default volume mesher's skin-depth guard remains unchanged; higher-frequency surface impedance is an explicit approximation with its own guard/provenance. Via return-contact inputs are rejected until the terminal adapter can model them explicitly.

title: Fix self-touching TOP/BOTTOM bus tuning and enforce route approval checks
description: The native TopBottom bus solver could generate tuning copper that retraces or touches itself, creating a shortcut through the matched trace length. This PR vendors the fix and adds PCB visual regression tests for all four copper layers. The vendored solver is pinned to source commit aa214adb66403c6be14acd5fea29432702fb97f5 (native solver 45(https:github.comtscircuitbus-lanes-solverpull45), main solver 44(https:github.comtscircuitbus-lanes-solverpull44)). Native complete-copper self-short auditing is mandatory at acceptance and after optimization, and benchmark approval independently rejects self-touching traces. The SBC physical audit covers crossings, touches, adjacent retraces, duplicate handoffs and untimed controls. Add SVG snapshot comparisons, matching GitHub-viewable PNGs, missing-baseline protection, and CI uploads of magenta snapshot diffs. bun run test:pcb checks the images; bun run snapshot:pcb explicitly updates them. See the four-layer PCB gallery(https:github.comtscircuitam3352-sbcblobfixreject-self-touching-ddrdocspcb-snapshotsREADME.md). DDR regeneration remains blocked. These initial snapshots show the inherited partial checkpoint, not newly accepted DDR routing. The existing DDR still uses inner layers. Three fresh searches against actual native fixed copper failed: the standard search exhausted its plans after 44 minutes, alternative ordering exhausted 30 minutes, and a bounded window exhausted 20 minutes. No new routes were promoted. The search summary(https:github.comtscircuitam3352-sbcblobfixreject-self-touching-ddrdocspcb-snapshotsregeneration.json) records the failures. A fresh routing comparison additionally requires complete timing, coupling and physical acceptance, including zero self shorts; snapshot:pcb-diff rejects the inherited routes. Fix the standalone DDR exporter to hydrate native fixed copper before compaction, matching live routing and including 79 missing inline-via obstacles. The hydrated fixed-copper baseline passes its physical audit with zero issues. Preserve authored fanouts, strict paired-prefix planning, timed-via limits and all DDR timing constraints. Validation: SBC routingsnapshot suite: 152 tests passed, 0 failed, including all four PCB snapshots. An intentional geometry mismatch was rejected and produced a diff PNG. Type checking, explicit snapshot-test type checking, frozen dependency installation and vendor integrity checks passed. Main solver after merge conflict resolution: 480 tests passed, and 1111 AM3352 benchmark layouts passed complete routing, DRC, TOTAL copper matching and self-short auditing. Native solver: 476 tests passed, with the completed native benchmark gallery(https:github.comtscircuitbus-lanes-solverblobfixreject-self-touching-nativedocsself-touching-guardREADME.md). Complete-board routing and manufacturing signoff remain outstanding. The images are review references for the partial checkpoint.
body:
The native Top/Bottom bus solver could generate tuning copper that retraces or touches itself, creating a shortcut through the matched trace length. This PR vendors the fix and adds PCB visual regression tests for all four copper layers.

The vendored solver is pinned to source commit `aa214adb66403c6be14acd5fea29432702fb97f5` ([native solver #45](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/45), [main solver #44](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/44)). Native complete-copper self-short auditing is mandatory at acceptance and after optimization, and benchmark approval independently rejects self-touching traces. The SBC physical audit covers crossings, touches, adjacent retraces, duplicate handoffs and untimed controls.

Add SVG snapshot comparisons, matching GitHub-viewable PNGs, missing-baseline protection, and CI uploads of magenta snapshot diffs. `bun run test:pcb` checks the images; `bun run snapshot:pcb` explicitly updates them. See the [four-layer PCB gallery](https://github.com/tscircuit/am3352-sbc/blob/fix/reject-self-touching-ddr/docs/pcb-snapshots/README.md).

**DDR regeneration remains blocked.** These initial snapshots show the inherited partial checkpoint, not newly accepted DDR routing. The existing DDR still uses inner layers. Three fresh searches against actual native fixed copper failed: the standard search exhausted its plans after 44 minutes, alternative ordering exhausted 30 minutes, and a bounded window exhausted 20 minutes. No new routes were promoted. The [search summary](https://github.com/tscircuit/am3352-sbc/blob/fix/reject-self-touching-ddr/docs/pcb-snapshots/regeneration.json) records the failures. A fresh routing comparison additionally requires complete timing, coupling and physical acceptance, including zero self shorts; `snapshot:pcb-diff` rejects the inherited routes.

Fix the standalone DDR exporter to hydrate native fixed copper before compaction, matching live routing and including 79 missing inline-via obstacles. The hydrated fixed-copper baseline passes its physical audit with zero issues. Preserve authored fanouts, strict paired-prefix planning, timed-via limits and all DDR timing constraints.

Validation:
- SBC routing/snapshot suite: **152 tests passed, 0 failed**, including all four PCB snapshots. An intentional geometry mismatch was rejected and produced a diff PNG.
- Type checking, explicit snapshot-test type checking, frozen dependency installation and vendor integrity checks passed.
- Main solver after merge conflict resolution: **480 tests passed**, and **11/11 AM3352 benchmark layouts passed** complete routing, DRC, TOTAL copper matching and self-short auditing.
- Native solver: **476 tests passed**, with the [completed native benchmark gallery](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/fix/reject-self-touching-native/docs/self-touching-guard/README.md).

Complete-board routing and manufacturing signoff remain outstanding. The images are review references for the partial checkpoint.

body:
Adds typed and validated props for `<simulation.pcbreturncurrentsimulation>` and its nested `<simulation.pcbreturncurrentexcitation>` elements, so PCB return-current experiments can be authored in TSX.

`simulationProps.pcbreturncurrentsimulation` and `simulationProps.pcbreturncurrentexcitation` expose the validators through a matching props namespace. Existing named schemas, TypeScript interfaces and module paths remain compatible. The guide and generated README use the namespaced JSX tags, with matching section anchors.

Authors select the signal driver/load and actual GND pads explicitly. `returnSource` is the load-side GND contact; `returnSink` is the driver-side GND contact. Current is a positive peak amplitude in amperes, and both port resistances are explicit real ohm values. Unit strings such as `5mA`, `25ohm`, and `100Ω` normalize to SI values. Missing contacts, invalid dimensions, nonfinite values, and unsupported props fail validation.

```tsx
import { simulation } from "@tscircuit/core"

<simulation.pcbreturncurrentsimulation name="DDR D13 return path">
  <simulation.pcbreturncurrentexcitation
    source=".U1 > .DDR_D13"
    load=".U2 > .DQ13"
    ground="net.GND"
    current="5mA"
    returnSource=".U2 > .GND"
    returnSink=".U1 > .GND"
    sourceImpedance="25ohm"
    loadImpedance="100ohm"
  />
</simulation.pcbreturncurrentsimulation>
```

The core implementation consumes these schemas to emit pending Circuit JSON definitions after PCB routing. These props do not connect pins or run a solver. Frequency and mesh/sampling parameters remain CLI run options because the current pending-experiment schema cannot store them. Initial return-contact selectors identify physical PCB ports/pads; standalone via contacts are not supported by the solver adapter.

Includes a usage guide and generated component, props, and README documentation. All four required generators were run.

Validation: all 654 tests pass, including six new tests for units, required contacts, layer inputs, and rejected run settings; typecheck, ESM/declaration build, formatting, and built namespace-export/SI parsing smoke test pass.

title: repro: regulator output inferred as required power
description: Fixes the incorrect inference of the VDD18 pin as a required power input in the USB2244-AEZG-06 SD-card controller, ensuring it is treated as an internal regulator output instead.
body:
## Motivation

The [USB hub board](https://tscircuit.com/gokul/usb-hub-board) uses the USB2244-AEZG-06 SD-card controller imported from JLCPCB part C333876.

Microchip identifies pin 13, `VDD18`, as an internal 1.8 V regulator output that should only connect to an external filter capacitor. The converter currently infers `requiresPower: true` from the `VDD18` label, so Circuit JSON describes this output as a required power input.

## Reproduction

| Stage | Current result |
| --- | --- |
| EasyEDA pin | Pin 13 is labeled `VDD18` |
| Generated TSX | Pin 13 receives `requiresPower: true` |
| Circuit JSON | Pin 13 has `requires_power: true` and no `provides_power` |
| Datasheet role | Internal 1.8 V regulator output |

![C333876 regulator-output snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/easyeda-converter/repro-regulator-output-power-direction/tests/convert-to-ts/__snapshots__/C333876-regulator-output-repro.snap.svg)

This PR adds the exact C333876 EasyEDA fixture and a focused snapshot test for the current behavior. It does not change converter logic.

## References

- [USB2244 hardware design checklist](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/UNG/ProductDocuments/DesignChecklist/USB2244-HW-Design-Checklist-00004319.pdf)
- [LCSC C333876](https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C333876.html)

## Validation

- `bun test tests/convert-to-ts/C333876-regulator-output-repro.test.ts`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`
