title: Support assembly reference surfaces and printed part color/material
description: Adds child assembly.referencesurface mounting anchors to generic and printed parts, then emits their resolved frames as cad_reference_surface records. For example, PART.anchor can position a board or printed part independently of the parts CAD geometry. Named JSCAD references also emit these records, and duplicate surface names are rejected across both forms. Frames use unit-aware centerXOffsetcenterYOffsetcenterZOffset, XYXZYZ planes, and perpendicular normalDirection values (x, x-, y, y-, z, z-). Optional paired widthheight survive serialization. Centers, normals, and X tangents follow finalized world placement, including inherited rotations and bottom-layer mounting. Geometry-free parts emit frames; model offsets do not move them. Schematic-only builds omit CAD records. Printed parts preserve optional color and material (pla, petg, nylon) on source records, with the explicit color override on CAD records. Imported models compose offsets inside their mounting frame. Includes usage documentation and an inspected JSCAD lamp visual: a base, hollow printed stem, tapered hollow shade with a collar and three spokes, and a bulb. The exploded and underside views enable showReferenceSurfaces to display named cyan mounting frames and orange outward normals. Validation: 63 assembly tests, TypeScript, and package build. Regression checks compare emitted frames with actual transformed probe geometry at 090180270 degrees on both layers, check tilted imported-model offsets, JSCAD reference frames, dimensions, repeat-render stability, and schematic-only behavior. The lamp test checks world mesh bounds, a hollow shade, and the 60 mm shade lift. Dependencies: tscircuitprops923 (merged; published props 0.0.697) tscircuitcircuit-json891 (merged; reference-surface schema) tscircuitcircuit-json889 (merged; published Circuit JSON 0.0.525) tscircuitcircuit-json-to-gltf244 (merged; using published renderer 0.0.151) All prerequisites are merged and published. Dependencies use tscircuitprops0.0.697, circuit-json0.0.525, and circuit-json-to-gltf0.0.151; no package previews remain.
body:
Adds child `<assembly.referencesurface>` mounting anchors to generic and printed parts, then emits their resolved frames as `cad_reference_surface` records. For example, `PART.anchor` can position a board or printed part independently of the part's CAD geometry. Named JSCAD references also emit these records, and duplicate surface names are rejected across both forms.

Frames use unit-aware `centerXOffset`/`centerYOffset`/`centerZOffset`, XY/XZ/YZ planes, and perpendicular `normalDirection` values (`x+`, `x-`, `y+`, `y-`, `z+`, `z-`). Optional paired width/height survive serialization. Centers, normals, and X tangents follow finalized world placement, including inherited rotations and bottom-layer mounting. Geometry-free parts emit frames; model offsets do not move them. Schematic-only builds omit CAD records.

Printed parts preserve optional `color` and `material` (`pla`, `petg`, `nylon`) on source records, with the explicit color override on CAD records. Imported models compose offsets inside their mounting frame.

Includes usage documentation and an inspected JSCAD lamp visual: a base, hollow printed stem, tapered hollow shade with a collar and three spokes, and a bulb. The exploded and underside views enable `showReferenceSurfaces` to display named cyan mounting frames and orange outward normals.

Validation: 63 assembly tests, TypeScript, and package build. Regression checks compare emitted frames with actual transformed probe geometry at 0/90/180/270 degrees on both layers, check tilted imported-model offsets, JSCAD reference frames, dimensions, repeat-render stability, and schematic-only behavior. The lamp test checks world mesh bounds, a hollow shade, and the 60 mm shade lift.

Dependencies:
- tscircuit/props#923 (merged; published props 0.0.697)
- tscircuit/circuit-json#891 (merged; reference-surface schema)
- tscircuit/circuit-json#889 (merged; published Circuit JSON ^0.0.525)
- tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf#244 (merged; using published renderer ^0.0.151)

All prerequisites are merged and published. Dependencies use `@tscircuit/props@^0.0.697`, `circuit-json@^0.0.525`, and `circuit-json-to-gltf@^0.0.151`; no package previews remain.

![Lamp mounting frames, exploded shade, and collar underside](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/assembly-reference-surfaces/tests/assembly/__snapshots__/assembly-reference-surface-lamp-annotated.snap.png)

title: preserve completed bus lanes across routing phases
description: Fixes full-board bus preservation failure by enabling the preserveOutputTraces flag for bus lanes, ensuring completed lanes remain as connected obstacles in later routing phases.
body:
### Motivation

### Before

### After
- Enables the existing `preserveOutputTraces` flag for `bus_lanes`, keeping completed lanes as connected obstacles in later phases. No new APIs or solver exceptions.

Examples include `hexnut_m3`, `hexnut_standard(din934)_m10`, `hexnut_imperial(1/4-20)`, and `hexnut_imperial(#6-32)`. Includes separate labeled ISOMETRIC, TOP, FRONT, SIDE snapshot baselines for [M3](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/blob/feat/metric-imperial-hex-nuts/tests/snapshots/__snapshots__/hex-nut-metric.snap.png), [1/4-20 UNC](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/blob/feat/metric-imperial-hex-nuts/tests/snapshots/__snapshots__/hex-nut-imperial.snap.png), and [#6-32 UNC](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/blob/feat/metric-imperial-hex-nuts/tests/snapshots/__snapshots__/hex-nut-numbered.snap.png).

These are nominal untoleranced visual models. Replace the preview dependency with the containing ModelPrinter release when published.

title: Add BallTransferUnit renderer and disable Bun lockfile saving
description: Adds BallTransferUnit for a captive load ball in a circular cup with a three-hole mounting flange, including rendering through Footprinter3d and React, and disables Bun lockfile saving.
body:
Adds `BallTransferUnit` for a captive load ball in a circular cup with a three-hole mounting flange. The model renders through `Footprinter3d`, React, and synchronous vanilla APIs, with no PCB pads. Public mesh and JSCAD geometry factories consume modelprinter's normalized dimensions and validation.

Includes closed housing and ball meshes, open mounting holes, numerical-resolution guards, an example, documentation, geometry/routing tests, and a labeled four-view PNG snapshot. Tests cover custom inch dimensions, zero socket clearance, matched sphere latitudes, mounting datums, and invalid geometry.

Disables Bun lockfile saving with `[install.lockfile] save = false` in `bunfig.toml`, removes the tracked `bun.lock`, and ignores both Bun lockfile formats. Publishing uses `bun install` rather than `--frozen-lockfile`. Fresh installs resolve the declared `circuit-json` 0.0.426 instead of the old lockfile's 0.0.232; the JST PH/ZH hole definitions now supply zero offsets/rotation, and the USB-C tab geometry handles an optional hole height.

Depends on https://github.com/tscircuit/modelprinter/pull/64. `package.json` pins its published preview at `fb0af29` so this PR installs independently; replace the preview with the released modelprinter version after that PR is merged and published.

Validation: lockfile-free `bun install --ignore-scripts` does not create a lockfile; typecheck, format check, and build pass. All 15 affected BallTransferUnit, JST PH/ZH, and USB-C tests and snapshots pass with the freshly resolved dependencies.

![Ball transfer unit: isometric, top, front and side views](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/69988e1da710a4f030902d3f57f21e97b382c43b/tests/snapshots/__snapshots__/balltransferunit.snap.png)

title: Use the ThreadedRod flag and boolean API
description: Adds support for left-handed and right-handed threaded rods with boolean API, rejecting enum-style string inputs and updating dependencies.
body:
ThreadedRod accepts dimensional tokens and `_lefthanded` / `_righthanded` flags, and uses `leftHand: boolean` in JSON after [ModelPrinter #63](https://github.com/tscircuit/modelprinter/pull/63). Read that boolean in the renderer while preserving default right-handed and explicit left-handed winding. Fixed construction fields are omitted, and enum-style string inputs are rejected.

Use the published `@tscircuit/modelprinter@0.0.20` release in the manifest and lockfile. Cover implicit right, explicit right, and left handedness through React and vanilla routing; assert enum-input rejection through all public entrypoints. The four-view snapshot uses the concise string label with unchanged geometry pixels.

Validation against the installed npm release: all 17 ThreadedRod numerical geometry, routing, rejection, and snapshot tests pass. Build, typecheck, and repository formatting pass.

title: Enable voltage divider, LED chain and parallel RC placement warnings

body:
Enable three existing placement analyzers in `checkSchematicPlacement`, so `runAllSchematicChecks` and `runAllChecks` report them as schematic component styling warnings.

| Analyzer | Warning |
| --- | --- |
| `VoltageDividerPlacementSolver` | The supply-connected resistor is clearly below the ground-connected resistor. |
| `SeriesLedChainPlacementSolver` | A series LED chain requires long connections behind LED pins. |
| `ParallelRcPlacementSolver` | A resistor and capacitor sharing a chip-pin/ground connection are drawn as staggered or crossed branches instead of adjacent parallel branches. |

Messages use readable component names. Each finding retains stable warning IDs and component, port, sheet, and subcircuit associations. Each new warning has its own TSX file with one test asserting that the fixture produces that warning.

Pins the analyzer dependency to `cece282ba71ba7466107a4243f27349500ba4a9d`, which includes LED-chain and parallel-RC detection. That revision also extends inverted-rail detection to positive-supply-to-signal resistors. Update the existing warning text to describe the supply pin facing down, without incorrectly calling the other pin ground. The pull-up fixture now faces its supply pin up, with a separate regression test for the inverted case.

Validation: 17 placement tests pass; TypeScript checking, build, Node import, packed-consumer smoke test, and formatting of the changed files pass.

title: Render reference surfaces on demand and honor CAD color overrides
description: Adds showReferenceSurfaces: true to GLTFGLB conversion, allowing named cad_reference_surface records to render as translucent rectangles with outlines, outward normal arrows, and PART.surface labels, while also honoring cad_component.color as a mesh color override.
body:
Adds `showReferenceSurfaces: true` to GLTF/GLB conversion. Named `cad_reference_surface` records render as translucent, double-sided rectangles with outlines, outward normal arrows, and `PART.surface` labels. The option defaults to false, works without an owner CAD model, respects explicit extents, and uses a 10 mm diagnostic rectangle for frames without extents. Browser conversion supports the same option.

Also honors `cad_component.color` as a mesh color override, preserving authored JSCAD opacity, roughness, metalness, and emissive settings.

Validation: all 72 unit tests pass; TypeScript and package build pass. Tests check emitted tilted-plane corners, normal arrows, label geometry, exported GLB transparency/double-sided materials, default-off behavior, and dimension fallback. PoppyGL snapshots in this PR cover the real hollow JSCAD lamp with reference surfaces off/on, the collar underside, frames without CAD models, and authored versus overridden CAD colors. Both snapshots were visually inspected; both snapshot tests and related unit tests pass.

Uses the merged reference-surface schema from tscircuit/circuit-json#891. Color overrides still depend on tscircuit/circuit-json#889; its immutable preview is rebased onto the merged schema. Replace the preview dependency with the published package before merging.


![Lamp reference surfaces: default, enabled, underside, and frames without CAD models](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/cad-color-override/tests/snapshot/__snapshots__/reference-surface-lamp.snap.png)

![Authored lamp colors and CAD color overrides](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/cad-color-override/tests/snapshot/__snapshots__/cad-color-override-lamp.snap.png)

title: Use outward winding consistently from loaders through GLB export
description: Ensures that Scene3D triangles face outward, their normals agree, and authored UVs stay attached to vertices, addressing inconsistencies in geometry representation across different formats.
body:
Scene3D currently mixes outward board geometry with inward CAD geometry. Untextured and material-grouped serializers reverse every triangle while the textured-board path preserves it, so identity-loaded models and untextured boards can face inward, and stiffeners expose their coplanar board-contact face.

Establish one contract: Scene3D triangles face outward, their normals agree, and authored UVs stay attached to vertices. Coordinate conversions now reverse winding only for reflections and transform normals with the inverse transpose. STL, OBJ material groups, JSCAD, cables and textured boards share a serializer that preserves triangle order. Rigid folding explicitly handles both reflection boundaries and their UVs. The final glTF X reflection keeps its own reversal. Shared flex-utils geometry and its correct stiffener conversion need no workaround.

Stacked on #246, which depends on #245. Merge in order #245 → #246 → this PR, retargeting each onto main after its base merges. This supersedes the compensating stiffener fix in #243.

Validation:
- Full Bun suite: 371 tests pass across 135 files; all existing image snapshots pass without updates.
- 243 focused tests pass, including 80 stiffener cases, 46 loader/export contract cases, folding, actual footprint/cable generators, panels and board-cut fallbacks. The new loader/export and stiffener cases produce 124 failures against the original main branch.
- Coverage checks actual loaded geometry and GLB accessors for winding/normal agreement, positive closed-solid volume, normal tangency and UV associations across identities, reflections, scales, rotations and folds. Actual STEP parsing is included.
- Rendered and visually inspected matching before/after GLBs from above and below; the corrected underside shows the full stiffener face.
- Full type checking, formatting and diff checks pass with declared dependencies.

title: fix: keep aligned ground rails clear of their labels
description: Fixes ground rail alignment to prevent overlap with their labels in schematic designs, ensuring that ground labels do not intersect with traces during layout adjustments.
body:
Stacked on repro PR #1305. Base: `codex/repro-tmc5160-gnd-label-overlap`. Merge the repro first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

Shared TMC5160 ground rails could be extended through their GND symbol during `traceCleanupSolver2`. Same-net labels were excluded from the general trace/label collision check, and later ground placement could leave the overlap unresolved.

Validate candidate rail alignments against ground-symbol interiors after considering the existing rail-end placement. Keep legitimate attachment-boundary contact and alignments whose ground label can move to a clear lower end. Restrict that lower-end search to the continuous vertical column attached to the label, so a separate GND branch at the same x coordinate is not mistaken for its destination.

The standalone core-captured input confirms this originates in schematic-trace-solver: the TST_MODE–SRBL and CLK–TST_MODE paths enter the label during rail alignment. Both the 11-pin reduction and full 49-pin capture now finish with no ground-trace intersections inside any GND label. The core reproduction also passes when loaded with the built solver bundle.

Rail-alignment collision protection and both ground-label placement paths use the same `getGroundNetIds` resolver. It resolves only declarations marked `isGround: true` to canonical connectivity IDs; net names and display text do not determine ground status. Labels are recognized by `globalConnNetId`, including labels whose `netId` is a different alias or is absent. Different ground nets remain separate.

Regressions cover aliases and unnamed labels with blocked and clear rail ends. Nets named `GND` with missing or false `isGround`, direct connections named `GND` without ground metadata, and unrelated nets displaying “GND” do not receive ground handling. The ground-placement fixture explicitly supplies `isGround: true`. Existing snapshots remain unchanged by the metadata-only correction.

Adds passing clearance regressions, blocked/clear rail-end and attachment-boundary coverage, a disconnected-column regression, and alias and metadata-only regressions. The rail-alignment fixtures use connectivity-map IDs rather than fabricated global net IDs. Two existing bug-report snapshots change only three GND label positions: they now remain attached to their host traces instead of jumping to a separate branch; their trace geometry is unchanged.

Validation:

- `bun test`: **700 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed** (704 tests / 304 files).
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: passed.
- `bun run test:package`: passed, including isolated Node, browser, and TypeScript consumers.
- Core integration with the built bundle: **2 passed**, checking every GND label in the reduced and full-chip cases.
- Formatting and `git diff --check`: passed.

![Fixed reduced reproduction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver/5a5c0c34c42881b9ffcbb2ec78b245f278fc9898/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-tmc5160-ground-bus-label.snap.svg)

[Full-chip snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver/5a5c0c34c42881b9ffcbb2ec78b245f278fc9898/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-tmc5160-ground-bus-full-chip.snap.svg) · [Original overlapping snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver/75cba96555f699682c133d0ba0a4e7f8b213142f/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-tmc5160-ground-bus-label.snap.svg)

Companion core repro: https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4471

The final schematic trace solver output places a shared GND label inside the TMC5160 ground bus. The TST_MODE–SRBL and CLK–TST_MODE traces cross the label interior despite belonging to the same net.

description: Fixes alignment of shared-pin branches with junctions to ensure correct geometry recognition regardless of route length or orientation.

The reproduction in #1256 shows a same-net branch whose junction marker is offset from the visible branch. The cleanup should recognize this geometry regardless of route length or orientation.

The C_XOUT branch turned beside the shared X2 junction, so the marker appeared on an otherwise straight wire. The first implementation limited the correction to paths containing exactly three and five points.

The alignment is selected from route topology: both traces must begin at the same pin coordinates, depart on perpendicular axes, and form compatible rails on the expected pin-facing side. Existing collision and net-label checks still validate every candidate.

- remove route point-count assumptions

- preserve routes whose endpoints do not occupy the same coordinates

title: Measure benchmark memory per isolated sample
description: This PR changes the benchmark memory measurement method to run each sample in a fresh process, allowing for accurate peak memory readings per sample instead of relying on a single process, which was affected by garbage collection.
body:
## Summary

The benchmark kept every sample in one Bun process, so garbage collection and retained heap from earlier samples changed later memory readings.

This PR runs each sample in a fresh process, records the OS peak memory for that process, and computes Memory P50/P80/P90 across those per-sample peaks. The PR table also shows each per-sample peak. Comparisons between the old and new measurement methods are marked as not comparable.

## Verification

- typecheck and format check pass
- all 145 tests pass
- two full SRJ18 runs completed all 8 samples with P80 335.1 / 339.4 MiB and P90 469.7 / 475.5 MiB

title: feat: detect transistor branches facing away from their supply rails
description: Detects incorrect rail orientation for transistors and provides placement advice without modifying the circuit.
body:
Stacked on the full-sheet TSX repro in #235. Both branches are rebased onto main with the native-transistor terminal fix from #234 merged.

Q1 and Q2 on the QRNG sheet point their positive-supply resistor branches left and their ground resistor branches right. `TransistorRailOrientationSolver` reports `TransistorHasIncorrectRailOrientation` and recommends rotating each transistor so those branches face up and down, then arranging the connected resistors and rerouting the traces. It emits placement advice; it does not modify the circuit.

Recognition requires a native three-pin NPN or PNP, three distinct non-rail terminal nets, and one unambiguous pair of opposite-facing ports connected through resistors to an explicitly positive supply and ground. It uses Circuit JSON flags, component types, source connectivity, and schematic pin geometry. It skips generic chips, missing/conflicting rail metadata, ambiguous branches or placements, different sheets/groups/subcircuits, invalid geometry, DNC terminals, and DNP parts. Names, labels, pin hints, and part numbers are not used to infer roles.

The existing full-sheet repro snapshot now highlights both transistors and their two rail resistors: six component markers with matching badges beside the two diagnostics. Its other diagnostics remain visible. The correction test changes placement properties on ten components across both stages, verifies identical electrical source records (excluding rotation-dependent display aliases), and renders the complete corrected sheet. The new findings fall from two to zero; existing findings fall from 18 to 11, with no new findings or collisions.

[TI Fundamentals of Analog Electronics Design, Figure 130, page 88](https://www.ti.com/lit/eb/slyy247/slyy247.pdf#page=88) illustrates supply-above/ground-below orientation. Its bias network differs from this project; the comparison concerns placement. The board is [AndyAguilo/qrng_optimized_dual-amp v0.0.1](https://tscircuit.com/AndyAguilo/qrng_optimized_dual-amp?version=0.0.1#schematic).

![TI reference on the left; original tscircuit TSX placement on the right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/6b109066b46363d0a06603fc422ce07a3398e891/reference-comparison.png)

![Original placement on the left; corrected placement with unchanged electrical connections on the right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/6b109066b46363d0a06603fc422ce07a3398e891/before-after.png)

[Full before sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/6b109066b46363d0a06603fc422ce07a3398e891/before.svg) · [Full corrected sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/6b109066b46363d0a06603fc422ce07a3398e891/after.svg)

Validation after rebasing onto main with #234 merged: 192 tests pass; typecheck and formatting pass. Tests cover the real TSX repro, its placement-only correction, PNP terminal ordering, removal of textual identities, directional rotations, missing/conflicting metadata, electrical shorts, ambiguous branches/placements, scope guards, and input immutability. No unrelated snapshots change in this solver PR; core rendering updates are isolated in #234.

title: test: reproduce sideways transistor stages on the full QRNG sheet

title: feat: detect chip supply inductors separated from their connected pin
description: Adds ChipSupplyInductorPlacementSolver, emitting InductorSeparatedFromChipPin for a native inductor placed far from its directly connected chip pin when the other terminal reaches an explicitly marked power net returning to the same chip.
body:
Stacked on #229, which contains the original full-sheet TSX repro.

Adds `ChipSupplyInductorPlacementSolver`, emitting `InductorSeparatedFromChipPin` for a native inductor placed far from its directly connected chip pin when the other terminal reaches an explicitly marked power net returning to the same chip. The Stride repro reports exactly L1 beside U1.

The rule uses component types, existing power/ground flags, connectivity and geometry. It requires a private two-port chip connection and a supply return to that same chip in the same local scope. It skips missing or contradictory metadata, shared signal nets, ground branches, ambiguous placements and DNC/DNP parts. It does not infer DCDC, converter or pin roles from names, hints, labels or part numbers. The spacing allowance is the larger of six schematic units or three inductor body dimensions; exact alignment is not required.

body:

title: Fix active native PCB text alignment
description: Fixes the vertical placement of active native PCB text strings to ensure proper alignment and visibility of evaluation warnings and caution labels.
body:
Native PCB strings with active top/center justification use a saved lower-left origin. Treating that point as the SVG anchor places PMP22712's evaluation warning too low and clips PMP23595's `CAUTION HOT SURFACE` off the left edge. This PR restores the warning's vertical placement and the full caution label inside the board.

- Read the modern frame flag with the complete extension-length guard and use the existing justification-valid flag.
- Align active free strings from their saved origin without using stale cached text widths. Apply the vertical correction in text-local coordinates so it follows rotation and mirroring.
- Cover real boards, all nine justifications with four rotations and both mirror states, stale widths, legacy/frame/ASCII guards, and unchanged binary round trips. The existing placement regression now checks the active origin correction; inactive free strings and frames explicitly retain the current-main behavior.

Independent PR against `main`, preserving the inactive-justification fix merged in #243. Arial font sizing is addressed separately by #245. Font metrics, layers, geometry and original reference images remain unchanged in this PR.

### Visual evidence

The existing side-by-side snapshots retain the real Altium reference on the left and render AltiumTS on the right:

- [PMP22712 evaluation warning](https://github.com/tscircuit/altiumts/blob/84d6c8d1b621e610dbf8bb06f979d6e328dedd32/tests/svg/__snapshots__/ti-pmp22712-pcb.snap.svg)
- [PMP23595 caution label](https://github.com/tscircuit/altiumts/blob/84d6c8d1b621e610dbf8bb06f979d6e328dedd32/tests/svg/__snapshots__/ti-pmp23595-pcb.snap.svg)

Six existing snapshots change relative to current `main`: PMP22650 (44 text records), PMP22712 (1), PMP22773 (34), PMP23595 (213), PMP23653 main (84), and its transformer (3). An SVG audit confirms only `y` and `text-anchor` change in these 379 text records; all other markup and reference pixels remain identical. The PCB snapshot inventory passes without changing its manifest.

Format evidence and the two native records are documented in `docs/format-references.md` and the focused regression test.

title: Fix native PCB text placement when saved justification is inactive
description: Fixes text placement issues in PCB designs by honoring the native validity flag for text justification, ensuring titles are fully visible and correctly anchored.
body:
PMP22712's resolved board title is centered across the left border because its modern native text record retains `JUSTIFICATION=5` even though that setting is inactive. Honor the native validity flag so the title starts at its saved origin and is fully visible. The same fix moves PMP22773's mirrored title back inside the board while preserving its rotation and mirroring.

This PR targets **main**, including the merged project-string fix #244 and real-Altium comparisons #256. It addresses the inactive-justification cause of **V03 (text placement)**.

## Changes

- Decode `JUSTIFICATIONVALID` from byte 240 of the modern Texts6 layout (properties length at least 252 bytes).
- Use the default lower-left alignment when the flag is explicitly false. Preserve active justification and the existing behavior for ASCII/shorter native records without the flag.
- Preserve text coordinates, font size, rotation, mirroring, and original binary bytes. No board-specific positioning overrides.
- Strengthen the real PMP22712/PMP22773 regression with resolved project titles, saved transforms, and exact source round trips. Minimal native records cover active/inactive flags, shorter layouts, and rotated mirrored text; the existing ASCII test still covers all nine justification positions.

## Real Altium comparisons

PMP22712 now displays the complete `PMP22712E2` title at its saved origin, rather than clipping its beginning against the left viewport edge. [Before this fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/altiumts/d0d0ef1e9951bf6f673bdde5e9e5260a7bddb87a/tests/svg/__snapshots__/ti-pmp22712-pcb.snap.svg).

PMP22773's title retains the mirrored orientation visible in the real Altium reference, with corrected anchoring.

![PMP22773: original real Altium reference beside corrected mirrored title placement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/altiumts/9bbcdfd0c4cf22a7faa9ab9138eec454b8b593c4/tests/svg/__snapshots__/ti-pmp22773-pcb.snap.svg)

Seven existing comparison snapshots change: the six TI boards and ST-Link Mechanical 7. An XML comparison with `main` confirms that **only `text-anchor` and `dominant-baseline` attributes differ**. Reference image bytes, text values, element order, other attributes, and geometry are identical. PMP22650 accounts for most snapshot lines because 1,098 text records have inactive saved justification.

This fixes the inactive-justification part of V03. Active-justification positioning remains a separate case: PMP22712’s evaluation warning and PMP23595’s caution text still differ from Altium. Font size/metrics (V02) also remain separate, so text can still extend beyond its label frame. The original reference pixels and comparison crops are retained.

## Validation

**Full GitHub CI: 358 passed, 0 failed**, including all AM62L tests ([successful run](https://github.com/tscircuit/altiumts/actions/runs/37811552094)). The GitHub merge tree was checked against the tested PR tree; it targets current `main` and contains no extra repro snapshot.

title: Use flags for ThreadedRod strings and JSON
description: Removes enum parsing and compatibility aliases for ThreadedRod, introducing boolean flags for handedness and updating JSON representation accordingly.
body:
ThreadedRod exposed enum-style selectors for fixed construction and handedness. Accept dimensional tokens plus `_lefthanded` / `_righthanded`, and represent handedness as `leftHand: boolean` (default `false`). JSON omits the fixed `spec`, `thread`, and `ends` fields.

Fully threaded construction and flat ends are intrinsic to the model. Validate duplicate or conflicting handedness flags before normalizing away `_righthanded`. Bare names still support `.params().fn` renderer dispatch; `.json()` requires dimensions.

Update documentation and contract tests to use the flag API and assert rejection of enum inputs. Companion renderer migration: [jscad-electronics #447](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/pull/447), pinned to the verified preview of this commit.

title: Fix gantry acceleration and deceleration ramps at 400 ms

body:

Both commands send ramp_ms:400; firmware derives acceleration from the target speed, avoiding the legacy acceleration ceiling that stretched high-speed ramps.

GOTO returns X first, then Y, in half steps with the selected speed and acceleration. Stop, Space/Escape, focus loss or a fault cancels the return and prevents the next axis from starting.

The existing half-step ramp, finite/braking step counts, explicit Stop commands, board-fault handling and connection/heartbeat handling remain in place.

Focus loss, settings edits and explicit stops clear the held input and stop motion; returning to the page and pressing again does not require rearming. Faults and missing/stale telemetry still block starts, with a specific reason shown on the page.

Stop now waits for fresh stopped-status telemetry before allowing another jog. Release completion waits for the deceleration/status acknowledgements, preventing old completion telemetry from prematurely clearing the active axis.

Validation: direct-jog regression tests cover pause recovery without rearming, no automatic restart, fault/stale gating, pending-stop interlocks and release races. Existing dashboard tests and all 36 firmware tests pass. No firmware update is required.

title: Ramp half-step gantry jogs on key press and release
description: Gantry jogging now uses continuous half-step motion: holding an arrow ramps to the selected maximum speed, and releasing requests a bounded firmware deceleration tail before coils release.
body:
Gantry jogging now uses continuous half-step motion: holding an arrow ramps to the selected maximum speed, and releasing requests a bounded firmware deceleration tail before coils release. The page includes holdable arrow buttons, active/coasting feedback, maximum speed and acceleration controls, and the estimated release distance. Defaults are 40 half steps/sec and 100 half steps/sec².

The additive `decelerate` command converts continuous motion into a finite braking tail and advertises `deceleration_supported`. Emergency Stop, Space/Escape, focus loss, stale telemetry, connection loss and board faults continue to release outputs immediately. Reversal waits until braking completes; older firmware cannot arm the new interface.

Validation: all 36 firmware tests, gantry regression tests, existing dashboard tests and JS syntax checks pass. Both connected RP2040/DRV8847 boards were updated, uploaded files were checked by SHA-256, and healthy telemetry confirms half stepping and deceleration support with motors stopped. Gantry X/Y names and alarm settings remain intact. No physical movement was commanded during validation.

title: Add two-board gantry keyboard jogging
description: Add a two-board gantry page at gantry.html, allowing users to connect two controllers for independent X and Y axis jogging using arrow keys, with safety features and telemetry checks.
body:
Add a two-board gantry page at `/gantry.html`, linked from the motor bench. Connect X and Y separately and hold arrow keys for repeated four-full-step jogs, defaulting to 20 steps/sec. Direction inversion and persistent USB naming are available per axis.

Jogging starts disarmed and stops both axes on key release, Space/Escape, focus loss, page hiding, stale telemetry, faults, or a move timeout. It waits for motion and completion telemetry between jogs. No homing, travel limits, or coordinated XY interpolation are provided.

Validation: keyboard-controller regression tests and existing dashboard tests pass. Both physical RP2040/DRV8847 boards report healthy protocol-3 telemetry with motors disabled. Physical movement has not been tested.

title: Detect repetitive staircase routing independently of odd angles
description: Add an independent PcbTraceStaircase rule to detect repetitive staircase routing in PCB designs, enabling detection of staircase patterns regardless of trace width or angle, and updating analysis results accordingly.
body:
The latest AM3352 board passes the existing odd-angle analysis despite extensive repeated stair-stepping. Add an independent `PcbTraceStaircase` rule enabled by default: the complete latest board now reports **181 staircase findings**, with their original copper highlighted in the SVG/PNG snapshots.

Detect at least six alternating bends over 2 mm between two consistent forward headings 15°–90° apart. Headings match within 4°, and merged steps must be at most 1 mm. Co-directed pieces merge before measuring steps or counting bends, so subdivision cannot fabricate bends or disguise long steps. Detection is independent of trace width, absolute angle, and the odd-angle thresholds; rotated staircases still match. Trace records, vias, pad interiors, and layer changes remain boundaries. These findings describe the routing style and do not establish that a replacement route would satisfy clearance rules.

Exposes rule selection and staircase thresholds in the library and CLI. Updates real-board results and snapshots to include both issue types; preserves the earlier complete AM3352 snapshot as an odd-angle-only regression.

Validation: 50 tests pass, including the latest board regression, subdivision/duplicate-point and rotation invariance, ordinary corners/arcs/meanders, topology boundaries, threshold/filter/artifact behavior, and 20,000-point input handling. Typecheck, formatting, browser build, and Cosmos site build pass. The repro regression intentionally fails without this fix.

title: Fix: analyze effective trace runs to prevent segmented-route bypasses
description: Fixes the analyzer to detect effective odd-angle runs that were previously reported as zero errors, specifically addressing issues with tiny route steps and allowed-angle staircases that bypassed length and angle checks.
body:
Tiny route steps can bypass the per-segment length check, and allowed-angle staircases can also bypass the angle check. On the linked AM3352 board, the analyzer previously reported zero errors; this change reports 44 effective odd-angle runs, including the 18.397 mm run in the stacked repro.

Stacked on [repro #7](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-pcb-style-analysis/pull/7). Merge the repro layer first, then retarget this PR to main.

Measure connected runs using iterative Ramer–Douglas–Peucker simplification within half the narrowest segment width. Preserve original physical checks, deduplicate findings covered by a failing run, and retain route ranges and constituent segments. Vias, pad interiors, layer changes, and separate trace records remain boundaries. An angular uncertainty allowance prevents small endpoint bends from turning allowed runs into false positives at strict tolerances. SVG and debugger highlights follow every original copper segment and use copper-inclusive bounds.

Includes the AM3352 debugger example and visual snapshot, subdivision regressions through 20,000 pieces, jitter and topology checks, and updated real-board expectations/snapshots. This also detects hidden runs in existing PD power supply (5 → 6 issues) and Corne keyboard (45 → 51 issues) fixtures.

Validation: 40 tests pass; typecheck, format check, browser build, and Cosmos site build pass. The complete linked board was checked before and after (0 → 44 issues). This PR is based on the repro branch; review its diff against that base.

The complete-board SVG snapshot asserts **44 detected issues** and checks that every original copper step belonging to those issues is highlighted. PNG previews render the same SVG snapshots.

body:
The standalone CLI could import C2040 but could not build a circuit. This adds `tsci build <entry>` using an embedded evaluator/worker, the offline platform, and local routing. A compiled executable now imports C2040 and builds a `src/` circuit using the generated component without project node_modules, tokens, or Bun/Node on PATH.

Builds produce Circuit JSON, PCB/schematic SVG previews, and a diagnostic report. Design-rule errors preserve those inspection artifacts and return status 1. Missing modules/parts and unsupported remote footprints/assets/providers fail locally before publishing new artifacts.

The loader follows a bounded local static source graph, supports ordinary TypeScript extension substitution, preloads Unicode-bound imports, and assigns unique virtual module paths to avoid eval's relative-import cache collisions. The worker replaces online provider defaults, captures swallowed async failures, and rejects custom parts engines and authored cloud routing.

Three examples and their inspection snapshots are included:

| Example | SMT pads | PCB traces | Vias | Core errors | Warnings |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| LED/resistor | 6 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 3 |
| RP2040 runtime fixture | 72 | 26 | 8 | 0 | 5 |
| Direct supplier footprint | 59 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 4 |

RP2040 regressions check all 57 U1 pads, routed 3.1 mm thermal ground, and geometric schematic continuity to power/ground labels. Inspection found an upstream automatic-layout ground-label omission; the RP2040 fixture uses explicit schematic placement as a workaround. Its source netlist was correct. The remaining warnings concern unsourced passives, intentionally incomplete supplier-chip metadata, and compact sheet sizing.

Validation: `bun run check` passes (63 tests, typecheck, binary compilation, and clean-directory binary smoke). [CI qualification](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/actions/runs/37892852019) passed native socket tracing with zero network attempts on the exercised success/failure paths, builds in a network namespace, and compilation/artifact upload for all five targets. Build artifacts include reproducible dependency notice inventories. Native qualification beyond Linux x64, complete runtime/WASM licensing, RunFrame/dev, simulation, catalog growth, and an official release remain planned.

title: feat: simulate receiver eyes and PCB crosstalk
description: Computes PCB crosstalk waveforms, receiver eyes and spectra from Circuit JSON, with paired switchingquiet-aggressor runs. Known-UI and authored-clock timing both produce eyes; authored clocks remain nominal references.
body:
Computes PCB crosstalk waveforms, receiver eyes and spectra from Circuit JSON, with paired switching/quiet-aggressor runs. Known-UI and authored-clock timing both produce eyes; authored clocks remain nominal references.

![Verified receiver eyes with switching and quiet aggressors](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/simulate-pcb-noise/8f655890801d3a870cecbf3f9a110a4877df1564/docs/images/receiver-eye-comparison.png)

The initial solver supports two straight, equal-width parallel traces over ideal ground. It extracts a quasi-TEM network with constant permittivity and finite-slab copper loss. [Model and API details](https://github.com/tscircuit/simulate-pcb-noise/blob/codex/pcb-crosstalk-noise/docs/model-and-api.md#physical-scope) state the physical limits. Failed numerical checks produce diagnostics without completed assets.

Compact TSX is shown in [props #927](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/927), with [core #4472](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4472) and [Circuit JSON #895](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/895). [README #2](https://github.com/tscircuit/simulate-pcb-noise/pull/2) adds the visual guide independently.

Local verification passed: 157 tests, typecheck, build, browser/Node/CLI consumers, and four installed demo cases with 82 numerical gates each. Their 138 assets reproduced the qualified outputs byte for byte. The latest documentation changes leave the verified runtime unchanged. The two added Actions workflows were removed; this PR adds no workflows.

title: Add visual README with verified crosstalk and eye plots
description: This PR adds a visual README that includes verified crosstalk and eye plots, enhancing the documentation and usability of the repository.
body:
The repository's default branch has only a starter README, so its purpose and results are hard to assess. This adds a concise visual guide with actual receiver eyes, raw crossing spread, victim waveforms and the two-line PCB view, plus a solver-to-renderer diagram and runnable example.

![Verified receiver eye comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/simulate-pcb-noise/8f655890801d3a870cecbf3f9a110a4877df1564/docs/images/receiver-eye-comparison.png)

The four images are byte-identical to verified simulation outputs. Their provenance records the input data, package pins, hashes and bounded physical model. Relative links, reproduction commands and captions were checked locally and independently reviewed.

This PR contains documentation and images only. It can be merged independently of the solver implementation in #1 and adds no GitHub Actions workflows.
